# A.I.R. Galleryʼs Downtown Manhattan Homecoming

Rendering of A.I.R. Gallery’s West Village lobby and library by OneFourTwo Architecture.

### A Once-in-a-Generation Capital Campaign to Secure the Future of a Historic Feminist Arts Institution

A.I.R. Gallery is at a transformational moment in its 54-year history.

After nearly two decades in Brooklyn, we are returning to our Manhattan roots and establishing a new, long-term home at the Federal Archive Building in the West Village. Our new 2,400 square foot facility will double the space devoted to our feminist programming and secure the future of one of New York City’s oldest alternative art spaces.

**A.I.R. is now undertaking a once-in-a-generation capital campaign to renovate our new home ahead of an early 2027 reopening.**

To learn more and make a contribution, [click the link here](http://airgallery.org/2026-capital-campaign).

#### Bill Arning Exhibiitions presents

## Great Art: Paintings by Donna Moylan, Andy Ness, & Erik Daniel White

#### NADA Miami 2026 | December 1–5, 2026

Presented at NADA Miami 2026, _Great Art_ brings together new paintings by Donna Moylan, Andy Ness, and Erik Daniel White, responding to Tim Dlugos’s poem of the same name, written while he was dying of AIDS. Exploring the intimacy of shared attention and the ways images become woven into our relationships, the artists draw on art-historical and cultural references, moments of ecstasy and quietude, and depictions of people looking together. Their works reflect on art, memory, and the passage of time, and on how returning to familiar images can bring us back to the people we have loved, the experiences we have shared, and those who remain with us in their absence.

[Learn more](https://www.billarning.com/great-art)

Erik Daniel White, _The Fall of the Rebel Angels, after Bruegel,_ 2026, oil on linen, 23 x 21 in 

Donna Moylan, _Artists in a Roman Gallery_, 2026, acrylic on muslin, 24 x 30 in

Sept 25, 2026–Jan 3, 2027

Frist Art Museum 919 Broadway, Nashville, Tennessee, 37203 Sept 25, 2026–Jan 3, 2027 Ingram Gallery Shimmer: Dreaming the Posthuman features 16 artists, including Marina Zurkow, working with both analog and emergent technologies to visualize the interrelationship between humanity, other species, and the earth itself. Using media such as digital animation, augmented and virtual reality, and artificial intelligence, artists challenge the view of human exceptionalism that prevents an ethics of care for the planet. Like the surrealists, these artists tap into the transformative agency of the marvelous, the uncanny, and the unpredictable. In their fluid and floating creations, images morph, flicker, and dance, forming psychologically charged archetypes within a new collective unconscious. Pictured: Marina Zurkow, Mesocosm (Wink, TX), 2012

[Details](https://fristartmuseum.org/exhibition/shimmer-dreaming-the-posthuman/?mc_cid=cd9d9cc53e&mc_eid=UNIQID)

September 12 - December 20, 2026159 Pioneer Street, Brooklyn.

Child/ren of the Bloom by LaJuné McMillian is an interactive, multidisciplinary installation that explores the threshold between land and sea, and the body's return to its origins. Developed alongside the artist’s 2026 OceanX Education's artist residency, piloted in partnership with Pioneer Works, the exhibition transforms her research on phytoplankton, algal blooms, and bioluminescence into a spiritual, embodied encounter with oceanic systems.

[Details](https://pioneerworks.org/exhibitions/lajune-mcmillian-child-ren-of-the-bloom)

[Rafael Lozano-Hemmer: Look AliveGeorgetown University Art Galleries](https://guartgalleries.org/exhibitions/46-rafael-lozano-hemmer-look-alive/)

September 18, 2026 - April 11, 20273535 Prospect St NW, Washington, DC 20007

Rafael Lozano-Hemmer: Look Alive presents a selection of installations by the internationally acclaimed Mexican-Canadian artist, whose work over the past three decades has explored the intersections of contemporary art, architecture, performance, and technology. Featuring the premiere of Pulse Map, the newest work in the artist's celebrated Pulse series, the exhibition invites visitors into responsive environments that evolve through light, movement, sound, and participation.

[Details](https://guartgalleries.org/exhibitions/46-rafael-lozano-hemmer-look-alive/) 

[timeframes_web-aspect-ratio-4-3](https://sjuartgallery.org/Siebren-Versteeg)CURRENT: OFFSITE

[Siebren Versteeg: TIME FRAMESYeh Art Gallery](https://sjuartgallery.org/Siebren-Versteeg)

September 24, 2026–Spring 202780-00 Utopia Pkwy, Jamaica, NY 11432

In TIME FRAMES, Siebren Versteeg presents five live-feed video artworks that transform familiar places through techniques of re-cropping, mirroring, pixelation, and other forms of digital manipulation. Installed on flat-screen monitors within the gallery’s hallway vitrines, each video is surrounded by a painted frame bearing the work’s title. Fabricated in collaboration with artist April Childers, the frames connect the individual works into a continuous visual poem along the corridor while extending authorship, along with the live video feeds, beyond that of the individual artist.

[Details](https://sjuartgallery.org/Siebren-Versteeg)

Established in 1973, Creative Growth Art Center is an internationally recognized nonprofit based in Oakland, California. It is the world's first independent art center dedicated to advancing the careers of artists with developmental, mental, and physical disabilities. Today, Creative Growth supports 140 artists, many of whom have sustained decades-long studio practices and exhibit widely in museums, galleries, and public collections around the world.

[LEARN MORE](https://www.creativegrowth.org/post/12496-50-years-of-creative-growth---key-milestones)

---

CURRENT EXHIBITION

STEREO DYNAMIC

ON VIEW FROM SEPTEMBER 18th - NOVEMBER 21ST, 2026

Stereo Dynamic is the ultimate visual mixtape! This group exhibition explores what happens when music fuels the making, featuring handcrafted instruments, music videos, customized vinyls, and hand-stitched portraits of musical legends. Join us to celebrate the tracks, icons, and beats that inspire the art. Opening night will feature live performances by Creative Growth artists, a live DJ set, and a glam rock window installation by Aurie Ramirez. ASL and Spanish interpretation provided. 

MEMBER PREVIEW: Friday, September 18, 5–6 PM

PUBLIC OPENING: Friday, September 18, 6–8 PM

ARTIST LED EXHIBITION TOUR:  Saturday, September 26th, 2:30–3:30 PM

CLOSING RECEPTION: Friday, November 20, 6-8 PM 
📍 Location: Creative Growth Art Center, 355 24th Street, Oakland, CA, 94612

[LEARN MORE](https://www.creativegrowth.org/post/19799-stereo-dynamic)

---

SPOTLIGHT EVENTS

Latefa Noorzai Solo Exhibition at Creative growth's gallery in Berkeley

November 12, 2026 - January 30, 2027 | by Collector Preview or appointment only

Join us for a special collectors’ preview celebrating Latefa Noorzai and her remarkable body of work. The exhibition features the last three remaining large-scale paintings on paper, presented alongside a selection of her later work. Together, these pieces offer a unique opportunity to revisit a significant chapter of her artistic practice and discover how her work continued to evolve. We look forward to welcoming you for an intimate first look at this special presentation.

[LEARN MORE](https://www.creativegrowth.org/post/20529-latefa-noorzai-solo-exhibition-at-cg2-in-berkeley)

---

SPOTLIGHT NEWS

CREATIVE GROWTH ARTISTS

SHINE ON NBC BAy Area

NBC Bay Area recently stopped by Creative Growth for a sneak peek at one of the designs heading to the runway during Oakland Style Week.

Reporter Velena Jones visited the studio to meet Creative Growth artist Elizabeth Rangel and learn more about her approach to fashion design. Rangel shared how her Mexican heritage inspires her work and how she turns the ideas in her imagination into wearable art.

For Rangel, fashion has been a lifelong dream. She’s been designing since she was a child, and today she’s bringing those early visions to life through Creative Growth’s Fashion Program. When asked what she would say to someone with a dream of their own, Rangel kept it simple:

“If you have a dream, don't let anyone take that away.”

[WATCH THE STORY](https://www.nbcbayarea.com/news/local/oakland-style-week-2/4151784/?_branch_match_id=1635727486359930161&utm_medium=share&_branch_referrer=H4sIAAAAAAAAA8soKSkottLXz0tKTkqsTCxKTdRLLCjQy8nMy9bP8E%2BMSi00dQw1S7KvK0pNSy0qysxLj08qyi8vTi2ydc4oys9NBQCaUDvRQQAAAA%3D%3D)

ARTIST SPOTLIGHT

WILLIAM SCOTT

View the process behind Praise Frisco: Peace and Love in the City, a work commissioned by SFMOMA as part of Creative Growth's landmark exhibition The House That Art Built. This piece captures artist William Scott’s optimistic vision of San Francisco, where his vibrant imagination transforms the city's architecture into an idealized urban landscape. Documented by Creative Growth staff, the creation of this work highlights Scott’s artistic journey, as seen in his Bay Area Walls mural. With bold colors and expressive brushstrokes, Scott conveys a hopeful and dynamic perspective of the city, celebrating peace, love, and community in his reimagined San Francisco.

[VISIT ARTIST PAGE](https://www.creativegrowth.org/artist/william-scott)

Visit The Creative Growth Art Center

Creative Growth Art Center is located in the Downtown/Lake Merritt area of Oakland, California. We are a 10 minute stroll to the lake. Our two-story tall art center was originally an auto shop and has tall ceilings and big windows. We are surrounded by still functioning auto shops, restaurants, newly constructed tall buildings, and a few historic homes. Our studio and gallery have separate entrances. The studio entrance is the most accessible for wheelchairs and other mobility aid users. Inside, the studio and gallery are connected by a long ramp. In the back of the studio there are accessible, gendered bathrooms. To access a single-stall gender neutral restroom, please ask a staff member. Outside, there is a wooden parklet to sit and rest in.

[LEARN MORE](https://www.creativegrowth.org/visit)

[CUE Art](https://cueartfoundation.org/)

## **_Open Kitchen 004: Bellhop 
_**Curated by Phil Zheng Cai 
Co-presented by Li Tang Community, Open Kitchen, and CUE Art 
November 19 – December 12, 2026 
Gallery Hours: Wed–Sat, 12–6 pm 
Service Requests (delivery of the exhibition to your doorstep!): Wed–Sat, 1–6 pm

## [Opening Reception](https://cueartfoundation.org/upcoming-events/opening-reception-open-kitchen-004-bellhop-curated-by-phil-zheng-cai): Thursday November 19, 6-8pm [\[RSVP\]](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeWuYTZzp37GhzNJxbVESJIZFW9KB6Pza9eu1UsJoB91eidKw/viewform?usp=dialog)

_“It is necessary to forget entirely one's intellectual culture, not in order to assimilate the work of art, but to deliver one's self up to it, heart and soul.”_ — Italian Futurist Painters' Manifesto, 1912

More than a century after the Italian Futurists called for the complete surrender of oneself to art, the language of delivery has acquired another decidedly less transcendent meaning. We deliver meals, groceries, packages, and increasingly, almost anything we desire, with the expectation that the distance between wanting something and receiving it should be as short as possible. Behind each seemingly effortless transaction is an elaborate choreography of bodies, infrastructures, and obligations. Someone must answer the calls.

_Open Kitchen 004: Bellhop_, curated by Phil Cai and organized in collaboration with Li Tang Community and CUE Art (and the first project of Li Tang Cypher), takes this logic to its absurd, and perhaps inevitable, conclusion: an exhibition that can be summoned to your doorstep upon request.

Read more about the exhibition [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/bellhop)**.**

---

Public Program: _Harvest Hantes_

Friday, October 16th, 7 pm – 12 am 

Join us for _Harvest Hantes: An Autumnal Celebration_, an evening of performance with alum artist Levon Kafafian grounded in the world of Azadistan, a futuristic society of their creation. The event, hosted in collaboration with Garod Collective, will include DJ sets by Armenian collective Hye Frequencies.

Tickets are sliding scale at the door. Advance RSVP is appreciated. Learn more and RSVP [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/upcoming-events/harvest-hantes)**.**

Public Program: _FONOTECA_:

Bring Records, Take Art

Wednesday, October 21st, 6–8 pm

Join us in the gallery for an evening of music, drinks, and collective archive building with artist Pablo Helguera in collaboration with The Clemente. The event contributes to _Fonoteca_, a new public vinyl library and listening room by Helguera. Bring vinyl to donate or lend in exchange for a limited edition artwork made by the artist for the occasion.

Learn more and RSVP [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/upcoming-events/fonoteca).

“Alternative Intimacy Simulation; or, A Hybrid Social Dance” by Juntao Yang

“Alternative Intimacy Simulation; or, A Hybrid Social Dance” by Juntao Yang, edited by Jinny Khanduja, was commissioned in conjunction with the solo exhibition _The Tropics, The Moon, and Mars_ by Mari Nagem as part of CUE’s Art Critic Mentorship Program. The essay is available online and in the exhibition catalogue.

Read the full essay [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/young-art-critics-essays/alternative-intimacy-simulation).

Closing Dinner: _Space Meal_

To mark the closing of _The Tropics, The Moon, and Mars_ by Mari Nagem, CUE commissioned and hosted _SPACE MEAL_, a roving multi-course dinner by artist and chef Tessa Liebman in conversation with the exhibition. Presented as an interplanetary meal of earthly provocations, the menu included seven vegetarian offerings drawing from themes and topics in Nagem’s works.

See photos from the event [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/the-tropics-the-moon-and-mars/#space-meal-photos).

Public Program: Curated Selects with Interspecies Library

On Saturday, September 19, CUE kicked off Climate Week NYC with a pop-up selection of books curated by Interspecies Library founder Oscar Salguero, presented in conjunction with our current exhibition, _The Tropics, The Moon, and Mars_ by Mari Nagem.

See photos from the program [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/the-tropics-the-moon-and-mars/#curated-selects-photos).

**Workshop: _Antenna_ with Thiago Hersan**

On Saturday, August 22nd, CUE hosted a jewelry-making workshop led by multimedia artist, engineer, and educator Thiago Hersan in collaboration with our current exhibition, _The Tropics, The Moon, and Mars_ by Mari Nagem.

See photos from the program [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/the-tropics-the-moon-and-mars/#program-photos).

**Opening Reception: _The Tropics, The Moon and Mars_**

On Saturday, July 11th, CUE opened _The Tropics, The Moon, and Mars_, an exhibition by Mari Nagem.

The exhibition is on view through Saturday, September 26th. Stop by during public hours (Wed–Sat, 12–6 pm) before it closes.

See more photos from the opening [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/the-tropics-the-moon-and-mars/#opening-photos).

**Opening Reception: _Datos Helados | Soft Tidal_**

_Datos Helados | Soft Tidal_ by Federico Bolagno-Romero & Mathías Chumino 
Curated by Will Rubenstein

On Saturday, June 6, CUE hosted the opening of _Datos Helados | Soft Tidal_, an exhibition by Federico Bolagno-Romero & Mathías Chumino, curated by Will Rubenstein with performances by Yellow Tears, Imminent Death, and Daren Ho.

See more photos from the opening [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/datos-helados-soft-tidal/#opening-photos).

**Opening Reception: _203 / H The Collector_**

On Saturday, May 23rd, CUE hosted the opening of _203 / H The Collector_, a group exhibition by Oorja Garg and Ridwana Rahman after a year of collectively reading Walter Benjamin’s _The Arcades Project_ with the Interdisciplinary Art and Theory Program. The exhibition emerges from questions of collecting, commodities, memory, and the strange afterlives of objects.

Learn more and see photos of the exhibition [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/203-h-the-collector)**.**

Collect available works from _mādar_: Iran Relief Exhibition

Browse available works, part of a collection contributed by 80+ artists in support of on-the-ground relief efforts in Iran organized by Melika Abikenari and Golnar Adili‍ in an exhibition at CUE.

See and collect available works [**here**](https://www.32auctions.com/organizations/138748/auctions/201094?r=1&t=all). 
Editions + prints also available in the [**_mādar_ shop**](https://cueartfoundation.org/madar-shop).

**Opening Reception: _mādar:_ Iran Relief Exhibition**

On Friday, May 15th, CUE hosted _mādar_, a group benefit exhibition and auction curated by Melika Abikenari and Golnar Adili. The exhibition features contributed artworks available for acquisition, with proceeds supporting humanitarian relief efforts through Moms Against Poverty and additional initiatives supporting people on the ground in Iran.

Learn more and see photos of the exhibition [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/madar-iran-relief-exhibition).

**—dirt— _earth_**

CUE Art and Peel, a Pittsburgh-based artist-run teahouse, hosted —dirt— _earth_, a one-night program by Tsohil Bhatia. Guests gathered for a shared meal in which the table became a site for speculation on the practices that have shaped what we consider palatable or objectionable.

Learn more [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/upcoming-events/dirt-earth).

Public Gathering: _What’s Left in the Remaking_

In conjunction with _What’s Left in the Remaking_, CUE hosted an informal public gathering to celebrate the thirty-one alumni artists and mentors in the exhibition. Participating artists lead a walkthrough and spoke about their ideas, practices, and contributions to the exhibition. 

See photos from the event [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/whats-left-in-the-remaking/#public-gathering-photos).

Opening Dinner: _What’s Left in the Remaking_

On Thursday, November 6th, CUE opened _What’s Left in the Remaking_, a group exhibition that brings together works by alumni artists and mentors of CUE

The exhibition is on view through Saturday, April 18th. Stop by during public hours (Wed–Sat, 12–6 pm) before it closes.

See more photos from the opening dinner [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/whats-left-in-the-remaking/#opening-photos).

Closing Program: _Boomerang_ by 
Jairo Sosa

To mark the closing of _Boomerang_ by Jairo Sosa, CUE hosted a closing program with tarot readings by Rei, food by Chef Tamarindo, and drinks by The Bronx Brewery +  the unveiling of Flashback, a new limited edition sculpture by Jairo Sosa.

See photos from the event [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/boomerang/#closing-photos).

_Boomerang_ Catalogue

The exhibition catalogue for _Boomerang_ is now available online and in print at CUE’s gallery space. Stop by to grab one!

This catalogue features texts by artist Jairo Sosa and mentor Hugh Hayden, as well as a catalogue essay by Alliyah Allen mentored by J Wortham as part of CUE’s Art Critic Mentorship Program.

Read the digital version [**here**](https://issuu.com/cueart/docs/boomerang_jairo_sosa).

“Transcending Ubiquity” by Alliyah Allen

“Transcending Ubiquity: Presence as a Means of Flight” by Alliyah Allen, mentored by J Wortham, was commissioned in conjunction with the solo exhibition _Boomerang_ by Jairo Sosa as part of CUE’s Art Critic Mentorship Program. The essay is available online and in the exhibition catalogue.

Read the full essay [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/young-art-critics-essays/transcending-ubiquity).

**_Flashback_ Limited Edition Sculpture** 

As part of _Boomerang_, a solo exhibition by Jairo Sosa, a limited edition of thirty ceramic basketballs titled _Flashback_ is available to order. Cast and glazed in one of nine different metallic glaze combinations, each sculpture carries subtle variations in surface finish and tone.

Proceeds from the edition support both CUE’s programs and the artist’s practice.

The works are available in person at CUE’s gallery space, or online at our [**shop**](https://cueartfoundation.org/cue-shop). 

Learn more and get one [**here**](https://jessica-gildea.squarespace.com/products/flashback-limited-edition-by-jairo-sosa).

**_Saplings_, presented by Forest For Trees**

_Saplings_ is a group exhibition organized by Forest For Trees that exhibits work by New York City youth, including alumni from the CUE Teen Collective. The show brings together young artists to amplify their perspectives on climate justice, and is now on view through August 31st.

Learn more [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/ctc-saplings-forest-for-trees).

**West Side Fest with Jairo Sosa**

During West Side Fest, CUE hosted a special program with exhibiting artist Jairo Sosa. Visitors were invited to meet the artist and enjoy vegan guava cheese ice cream, a flavor collaboration with Sosa made by artist Paul John as part of his community project @ijsmaaker. 

See photos from the event [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/boomerang/#public-program-photos).

**Opening Reception: _Boomerang_ by Jairo Sosa**

On Thursday, June 26th, CUE opened _Boomerang_, a solo exhibition by Jairo Sosa. Sosa was nominated for the opportunity by artist Hugh Hayden.

The exhibition is on view through Sunday, September 7th. Stop by during public hours (Wed–Sat, 12–6 pm) before it closes.

See more photos from the opening [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/boomerang/#opening-photos).

**Become a Member of CUE**

Join CUE’s new membership program and connect with a dynamic community of artists and supporters. Members receive exclusive benefits, including professional development opportunities, special events, and more.

Membership directly supports CUE’s mission—championing artist-centered programs, fostering critical discourse, and providing resources that empower artists.

Learn about levels and benefits [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/support-cue#membership).

**CUE Teen Collective: _Framing Lives_**

_Framing Lives_ was the final exhibition of the 2024-25 CUE Teen Collective. Rooted in the everyday, the works presented by student artists in _Framing Lives_ invited us to reconfigure the lenses through which we view ourselves and each other.

See photos from the exhibition [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/ctc-framing-lives/#artist-portraits). 
Learn more about the CUE Teen Collective [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/cue-teen-collective).

NADA New York

For the 11th edition of NADA New York, CUE presented a collaborative installation by artists Levon Kafafian, Fatemeh Kazemi, and Levani, coinciding with the final weekend of their group exhibition _The Bride Has Gone to Pick Flowers_. Together, the artists delve into the rich tapestry of cultural traditions from the Caucasus—reorienting, speculating upon, dreaming about, and queering inherited rituals in ways that embrace notions of fluidity and exchange.

Learn more and see photos [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/nada-new-york-2025/#installation-photos).

**_The Bride Has Gone to Pick Flowers_ Catalogue**

The exhibition catalogue for _The Bride Has Gone to Pick Flowers_ is now available online and in print at CUE’s gallery space. Stop by to grab one!

The catalogue features texts by artists Levon Kafafian, Fatemeh Kazemi, and Levani; curator Lila Nazemian; and mentor Martha Joseph; as well as a catalogue essay by Tsovinar Kuiumchian, mentored by Kim Córdova for CUE’s Art Critic Mentorship Program.

Read the digital version [**here**](https://issuu.com/cueart/docs/the_bride_has_gone_to_pick_flowers_lila_nazemian).

**Mirror of Fate**

As part of the final week for _The Bride Has Gone to Pick Flowers_, CUE hosted a closing celebration with artist Levon Kafafian entitled Mirror of Fate. The event included a performance by Kafafian and DJ set by 8ULENTINA, alongside small bites by Chef Sebouh Yacoubian of Taline and drinks by Vogis Gin and Back Home Beer.

See photos from the event [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/the-bride-has-gone-to-pick-flowers/#public-program-photos).

“Rewriting the Vow” by Tsovinar Kuiumchian

“Rewriting the Vow: Queer Visions of Marriage Rituals from the Caucasus” is a longform essay by Tsovinar Kuiumchian with mentorship from Kim Córdova as part of CUE’s Art Critic Mentorship Program. It was commissioned for the group exhibition _The Bride Has Gone to Pick Flowers_, curated by Lila Nazemian. The essay is available online and in the exhibition catalogue.

Read the full essay [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/young-art-critics-essays/rewriting-the-vow)**.**

_Resistance_ Limited Edition Tote Bags

As part of [_measuring the sounds of our resistance_](https://cueartfoundation.org/upcoming-events/measuring-the-sounds-of-our-resistance), hosted by exhibiting artist Levani_,_ a series of four unique limited edition tote bags made in Georgia and produced by QEDI (Democratic Initiative of Georgian Emigrants) are available to order. Proceeds support the student resistance movement in Georgia.

The bags feature original illustrations by Nonnie Gardava. They are available in person at CUE's gallery space, or online at our [**shop**](https://cueartfoundation.org/cue-shop).

Learn more and get one [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/products/limited-edition-tote-levani).

Screening + Listening Session: measuring the sounds of our resistance

In conjunction with _The Bride Has Gone to Pick Flowers_, CUE hosted a screening, listening session, and open dialogue hosted by artist Levani. The meditative event invited guests to reflect on global struggles and develop a shared understanding of resistance as embodied practice.

See photos from the event [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/the-bride-has-gone-to-pick-flowers/#public-program-photos).

**A Performative Dinner: Hearts of Sugar, Fingers Dipped in Honey**

In conjunction with _The Bride Has Gone to Pick Flowers_, CUE hosted a special performative dinner event by Fatemeh Kazemi and the food collective Bazm. The event included a five-course meal and various rituals and gestures contemplating the myth of the bride—one who has left without saying goodbye. 

See photos from the event [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/the-bride-has-gone-to-pick-flowers/#public-program-photos).

**Opening Reception: _The Bride Has Gone to Pick Flowers_**

On Thursday, January 30th, CUE opened _The Bride Has Gone to Pick Flowers_, a group exhibition curated by Lila Nazemian presenting works by artists Levon Kafafian, Fatemeh Kazemi, and Levani.

The exhibition is on view through Saturday, May 10th. Stop by during public hours (Wed–Sat, 12–6 pm) before it closes.

See more photos from the opening [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/the-bride-has-gone-to-pick-flowers/#opening-photos).

Closing Program: _This Fire That Warms You_ by Tsohil Bhatia

To mark the closing of _This Fire That Warms You_ by Tsohil Bhatia, CUE hosted a closing program with a performance and a viewing of a new video work.

Bhatia used their body and various objects to create impressions in flour. The remnants created a new ephemeral work that left a trace of their presence in the gallery, and remained on view until closing.

See photos from the event [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/this-fire-that-warms-you/#closing-program-photos).

Exhibition Video: _This Fire That Warms You_

Watch a short film with Tsohil Bhatia by Sunset People Productions to learn more about their background and practice as an artist and homemaker.

Bhatia reflects on labors of care in the kitchen, the concept of fire and the multiplicities it contains, and the notion of decay as related to mourning of the body.

Check out the video as well as other films from CUE’s recent solo exhibitions [**here**](https://vimeo.com/showcase/10720577).

_This Fire That Warms You_ Catalogue

The exhibition catalogue for _This Fire That Warms You_ is now available online and in print (for free) at CUE’s gallery space. Stop by to grab one!

The catalogue features texts by artist Tsohil Bhatia and mentor Puppies Puppies (Jade Guanaro Kuriki-Olivo), as well as a catalogue essay by Swagato Chakravorty, mentored by Alpesh Kantilal Patel as part of CUE’s Art Critic Mentorship Program.

Read the digital version [**here**](https://issuu.com/cueart/docs/this-fire-that-warms-you).

**Dinner with Red Flower Collective: Eight New Sculptures**

In celebration of _This Fire That Warms You_ by Tsohil Bhatia, CUE hosted a special dinner with Red Flower Collective. The event featured eight new ephemeral sculptures on view only for the dinner, as well as an eight-course dinner prepared on site, drinks, a limited edition menu by artist Rujuta Rao, and the launch of the exhibition catalogue.

See photos from the event [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/this-fire-that-warms-you/#dinner-program-photos).

“Latent Energies” by Swagato Chakravorty

“Latent Energies” by Swagato Chakravorty, mentored by Alpesh Kantilal Patel, was commissioned in conjunction with the solo exhibition _This Fire That Warms You_ by Tsohil Bhatia as part of CUE’s Art Critic Mentorship Program. The essay is available online and in the exhibition catalogue.

Read the full essay [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/young-art-critics-essays/latent-energies).

**Food Activation by Tsohil Bhatia x Red Flower Collective**

As part of the programming for NADA House, CUE presented a food-based activation by Tsohil Bhatia for Red Flower Collective, a communal eating and research collective of which they are a co-founder. The artist made three dishes and served them free to the public on the porch of NADA House.

Bhatia’s sculptural work, _Untitled (Rano)_, will remain on view at NADA House through October 27th.

See photos from the activation [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/nada-tsohil-bhatia#public-program-photos).

Opening Reception: _This Fire That Warms You_ by Tsohil Bhatia

On Thursday, September 5th, CUE opened _This Fire That Warms You_, a solo exhibition by Tsohil Bhatia. Bhatia was awarded the opportunity through CUE’s annual open call for solo exhibitions.

The exhibition is on view through Saturday, October 19th. Stop by during public hours (Wed–Sat, 12–6 pm) before it closes.

See more photos from the opening [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/this-fire-that-warms-you/#opening-photos).

**_Untitled (Rano)_ by Tsohil Bhatia**

A sculptural work presented as part of NADA House 
Project Dates: September 3 – October 27, 2024

In conjunction with the solo exhibition _This Fire That Warms You_ by Tsohil Bhatia, CUE presents a sculpture by the artist, _Untitled (Rano),_ at Nolan Park House 17 on Governors Island. The work extends the language of the domestic into the public realm, contemplating the artist’s decaying body and mourning the inevitable loss of time and its bodily manifestations.

Learn more and see photos [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/nada-tsohil-bhatia).

Closing Program: _Luma_ by Catalina Tuca

To mark the closing of _Luma_ by Catalina Tuca, CUE hosted a closing program with participatory engagements that responded to and engage with the ideas in Tuca’s solo show around memory, identity, violence, and nature. 

The program included a performance by artist María Verónica San Martín, herbalist Antonia Estela Pérez, and food by chef Oscar Riquelme.

See photos from the event [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/luma/#closing-photos).

Exhibition Video: _Luma_

Watch a short film with Catalina Tuca by Sunset People Productions to learn more about the artist’s background and practice.

Tuca speaks about her interest in objects and how they became part of her practice, the story of the luma and its relationship to the collective memory of Chileans of her generation, and the potential to create new narratives for material culture.

Check out the video as well as other films from CUE’s recent solo exhibitions [**here**](https://vimeo.com/showcase/10720577).

_Luma_ Catalogue

The exhibition catalogue for _Luma_ is now available online and in print (for free) at CUE’s gallery space. Stop by to grab one!

The catalogue features texts by artist Catalina Tuca and mentor Esperanza Mayobre, as well as a catalogue by Alexandra Trujillo Tamayo, mentored by Aimé Iglesias Lukin as part of CUE’s Art Critic Mentorship Program.

Read the digital version [**here**](https://issuu.com/cueart/docs/luma).

“Luma, Between Memory and Contemplation” by Alexandra Trujillo Tamayo

“Luma, Between Memory and Contemplation” by Alexandra Trujillo Tamayo, mentored by Aimé Iglesias Lukin, was commissioned in conjunction with the solo exhibition _Luma_ by Catalina Tuca as part of CUE’s Art Critic Mentorship program. The essay is available online and in the exhibition catalogue.

Read the full essay [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/young-art-critics-essays/luma-between-memory-and-contemplation).

**Opening Reception: _Luma_ by Catalina Tuca**

On Thursday, June 20th, CUE opened _Luma_, a solo exhibition by Catalina Tuca. Tuca was awarded the opportunity through CUE’s annual open call for solo exhibitions.

The exhibition is on view through Saturday, August 10th. Stop by during public hours (Wed–Sat, 12–6 pm) before it closes.

See more photos from the opening [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/luma/#opening-photos).

2023-24 CUE Teen Collective: 13 degrees of separation

_13 degrees of separation_ was the seventh annual exhibition of the CUE Teen Collective (CTC). This group show presented works by thirteen young artists that reflect upon their collective and individual identities. Through painting, drawing, installation, sculpture, mixed media, and video, students considered the many influences that unite and distinguish them.

Learn more and see photos [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/ctc-13-degrees-of-separation/).

Closing Event:

Kamayan Dinner + Banig Karaoke

To mark the closing of _Sometimes My Accent Slips Out_ by Bhen Alan, CUE hosted a special kamayan dinner celebration in the gallery by Chefs Woldy Reyes and LJ Almendras. Kamayan (“by hand”) is an intimate, communal feast with a longstanding precolonial history in the Philippines.

The dinner, co-hosted by Jon Santos, also featured a ritual and a performance by the artist, and was followed by a karaoke night that made use of his large-scale woven work as a projection screen.

See photos from the event [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/sometimes-my-accent-slips-out/#closing-photos).

Exhibition Video: _Sometimes My Accent Slips Out_

Watch a short film with Bhen Alan by Sunset People Productions to learn more about the artist's background and practice. 

Alan speaks about his personal history with weaving in the Philippines, the significance of language in his practice, and the influence of new ecologies on the materiality of his works. 

Check out the video as well as other films from CUE's recent solo exhibitions [**here**](https://vimeo.com/showcase/10720577).

_Sometimes My Accent Slips Out_ Catalogue

The exhibition catalogue for _Sometimes My Accent Slips Out_ is now available online and in print (for free) at CUE’s gallery space. Stop by to grab one!

The catalogue features texts by artist Bhen Alan and mentor Jade Yumang, as well as a catalogue essay by Sasha Cordingley, mentored by Ana Tuazon as part of CUE’s Art Critic Mentorship Program.

Read the digital version [**here**](https://issuu.com/cueart/docs/sometimes-my-accent-slips-out).

Ling-lin Ku at NADA New York

For the 10th edition of NADA New York, CUE presented a new sculpture work by Ling-lin Ku following her solo show at CUE. The work that was on view at NADA, _Invisiphilia_, is a digitally fabricated sculpture that playfully interrogates the disorienting experience of navigating digital spaces.

Learn more and see photos [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/nada-ling-lin-ku?mc_cid=ffb26e04c3&mc_eid=UNIQID).

“In the Folds” by Sasha Cordingley

“In the Folds” by Sasha Cordingley, mentored by Ana Tuazon, was commissioned in conjunction with the solo exhibition _Sometimes My Accent Slips Out_ by Bhen Alan as part of CUE’s Art Critic Mentorship Program. The essay is available online and in the exhibition catalogue.

Read the full essay [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/young-art-critics-essays/in-the-folds).

Opening Reception:

_Sometimes My Accent Slips Out_

On Thursday, April 4th, CUE opened _Sometimes My Accent Slips Out_, a solo exhibition by Bhen Alan. Alan was awarded the opportunity through CUE’s annual open call for solo exhibitions.

The exhibition is on view through Saturday, May 18th. Stop by (Wed–Sat, 12–6 pm) before the show closes.

See more photos from the opening [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/upcoming-events/sometimes-my-accent-slips-out).

Montez Press Radio: on _worried notes_

Tune into Montez Press Radio for a broadcast with artist Keli Safia Maksud and artist, filmmaker, and writer Christian Nyampeta. Maksud and Nyampeta discuss ideas embedded in _worried notes_, Maksud’s recent solo exhibition at CUE, and expand on themes of national identity and the formation of postcolonial Africa through the lens of music and cinema.

Learn more and listen [**here**](https://radio.montezpress.com/#/show/3348).

Exhibition Video: _worried notes_

Watch a short film with Keli Safia Maksud by Sunset People Productions to learn more about the artist's background and practice. 

Maksud speaks about the evolution of her interest in national anthems, the politics of drawing and line-making, and how her use of embroidery on carbon paper functions as a refusal of these systems.  

Check out the video as well as other films from CUE's recent solo exhibitions [**here**](https://vimeo.com/showcase/10720577).

_worried notes_ Exhibition Catalogue

Check out the exhibition catalogue for _worried notes_ by Keli Safia Maksud, now available online, and stop by CUE’s gallery space to pick up a free print copy.

The catalogue features texts by artist Keli Safia Maksud and mentor Abigail DeVille, as well as a catalogue essay by Jordan Jones, mentored by Renee Gladman as part of CUE’s Art Critic Mentorship Program.

Read the full essay digital version [**here**](https://issuu.com/cueart/docs/worried-notes).

“A Series of Openings—or, Ways of Worrying a Score” by Jordan Jones

“A Series of Openings—or, Ways of Worrying a Score” by Jordan Jones, mentored by Renee Gladman, was commissioned in conjunction with the solo exhibition _worried notes_ by Keli Safia Maksud as part of CUE’s Art Critic Mentorship Program. The essay is available online and in the exhibition catalogue.

Read the full essay [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/young-art-critics-essays/a-series-of-openings).

Limited Edition _Vendah_ Tote Bag

As part of _Vendah_, CUE has released a limited edition screenprinted tote bag with artwork by Cornelius Tulloch and graphic design by Jenni Oughton. 

The design references a new work by the artist, _Reapings of the Labored_, on view as part of the exhibition. 

Tote bags are available in person at CUE's gallery space, or online at our [**shop**](https://cueartfoundation.org/cue-shop).

For more information and to purchase, see [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/products/limited-edition-tote-cornelius-tulloch).

We’re Hiring!

CUE is now hiring for a number of exciting opportunities across our organization!

For position descriptions and details on how to apply, [**click her**](https://cueartfoundation.org/job-openings)**e**.

**Jinny Khanduja Named Executive Director**

CUE Art Foundation is thrilled to announce the appointment of Jinny Khanduja to the position of Executive Director.

Jinny comes to CUE from Storefront for Art and Architecture. She has worked for more than a decade at non-profit organizations cultivating mission-driven work in architecture, art, urbanism, and policy. At CUE, she will oversee the organization’s strategic vision and its programs.

Read more [**here**](https://cueartfoundation.org/updates-news/cue-art-foundation-appoints-jinny-khanduja-as-executive-director).
