## Dana DeGiulio

Dana DeGiulio (b. 1978 Chicago Heights, IL) works in various media ranging from painting, drawing, video, photography, installation and writing. In her work she often blurs the line between form and abstraction, body and space, object and voids, and does so with a painterly hand that conveys a depth of emotions from poignancy to rage to beauty and ethereality. Often working in series, Degiulio will present works focusing on the body in space for this exhibition.

Degiulio is an associate professor of painting at Rhode Island School of Design (RISD). She received her BFA and MFA from The School of the Art Institute of Chicago (SAIC) and has spent nearly twenty years teaching visual art to graduate and undergraduate students at RISD, NYU, Columbia University, and SAIC. She has also been resident faculty at the Skowhegan School of Painting and Sculpture in 2024, and last year delivered visiting artist talks at Yale, Rutgers, and the Schwules LGBTQ+ Museum in Berlin.

Her work has appeared in The New York Times, Artforum, erev rav, Impulse Magazine, Mousse Magazine, The Brooklyn Rail, Contemporary Art Daily, Bad at Sports, NewCity Chicago, on the Open Space Platform at SFMoMA, amongst other publications. Recently she’s solo exhibitions at the Ezra + Cecile Zilkha Gallery at Wesleyan University, Middleton CT, and PPOW in NY, NY. Previously she exhibited at commercial galleries, artist-run spaces, and numerous alternative venues.

[view Dana's full biography](https://outerspacearts.xyz/pdfs/danadegiulio_cv.pdf)

---

## Michelle Grabner

Michelle Grabner (b.1962, Oshkosh, Wisconsin) lives and works in Milwaukee, WI; Chicago, IL; and Waupaca County, WI. Her work focuses on process, repetition, pattern, and challenging notions between fine art and craft, and the meaning of everyday materials. Not limited to one medium, Grabner shifts between painting, drawing, weaving, sculpture and installation. For this exhibition she will present an installation of hand painted porcelain sculptures of various foods such as cabbage and potatoes.

Not only known for her art, Grabner also writes, curates, and teaches fine art. As an artist She has exhibited her work in galleries nationally and internationally and has had solo museum exhibitions at The Museum of Contemporary Art, Cleveland and The Indianapolis Museum of Art. In 2021, Grabner was named a Guggenheim Fellow by The John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation. She is represented by James Cohan, New York and Green Gallery, Milwaukee. In 2014 she co-curated The Whitney Biennial and in 2018 FRONT International: Cleveland Triennial for Contemporary Art. Grabner is the Crown Family Professor of Art and the Senior Chair of the Painting and Drawing Department at the School of the Art Institute of Chicago, where she has taught for 30 years. Previously, She’s held teaching appointments at The University of Wisconsin-Madison, Cranbrook Academy of Art; Milton Avery Graduate School of Arts—Bard College; Yale University School of Art; and the Skowhegan School of Painting and Sculpture, Maine.

Her work is included in numerous prestigious institutions including The Art Institute of Chicago, Chicago, IL, The Walker Art Center, Minneapolis, MN, Milwaukee Art Museum, Milwaukee, WI, Museum of Fine Arts Boston, Boston, MA, RISD Museum of Art, Providence, RI, Indianapolis Museum of Art, Indianapolis IN, ICA Boston, Boston, MA, Victoria and Albert Museum, London, UK amongst many others.

# **Maija Luutonen 
_Solitaire_**

For her second solo presentation at NOON Projects in Los Angeles, Finnish artist Maija Luutonen offers an intimate, site-specific installation bringing together paintings, artist’s books, and ceramic objects. Her work deals with the act and experience of perceiving the surrounding world. The paintings may be seen as condensed experiences of unraveling a perceived view or visual detail from underneath, above, or perhaps from the inside out. In “Solitaire,” perception becomes an intimate, embodied experience: an invitation to look closely, hold a painting, and spend time in the company of these objects. 

On view through December 19, 2026

### **Main Space**

**_Empathy's Alchemy_**Curated by Zahar Vaks 
November 7 - December 20, 2026 
Opening Reception: Saturday, November 7th | 6:00 - 8:00pm

Ortega y Gasset Projects (OyG) is proud to present  _Empathy's Alchemy,_ a show exploring the symbiotic relationship between empathy and alchemy within the works of [Ethan Greenbaum](https://www.ethangreenbaum.com/), [Mónica](http://monicapalma.com/), [Newton Pottinger, Kemar Wynter](https://www.instagram.com/kibbayamout/), and [Sun You](https://sunyou.us/index.html) . The opening reception will take place on Saturday, November, 7th , 2026 from 6-8pm, and run through December 20th, 2026.

I've been thinking about the Latin root of the word curator: cura, meaning "to take care." 

Over the years I have come to appreciate more and more how my curating process is connected to my creative practice. I am drawn to artwork on an instinctual level–a vibe, a resonance, a trace. I can't quite place it, and that is what excites me. It is an initial feeling that I follow–and through the following of that feeling I get a sense of understanding.

This has always been my practice; believing and leaning into what I don't necessarily understand. Trusting, leaping, dancing. Higher-level thinking happens after the fact, but the creative act itself is generally a blank zone, a state of intuition. Like meditation, dropping in.

This is a state of openness. A yearning to connect. A desire to collaborate. A moment to appreciate thinking through making.

Reflecting through the process of putting together this show, which pulls from so many experiences and influences, I can only say this: something can be specific but not fully developed, which then continues to evolve because of the things you decide to let in. When you say yes. When you are open.

Sometimes you have to block shit.

When you are open and when you trust what's coming in, it can both change things and still maintain the integrity of the original thing.

That's jazz.

That's freestyle.

That's improvisation.

But there is still structure to it.

Similar to the work of an educator. You have a plan but things happen and you have to adapt.

This is creation. 

This is curation.

This is life. 

It was through this process, following instincts, remaining open, and paying attention to what continued to resonate, that _Empathy's Alchemy_ began to take shape.

What interests me about empathy is its vastness. Sometimes it is linked to a specific story. Other times it exists in more subtle ways, as a non-verbal and yet undeniably present experience. It can emerge through narrative, but it can also emerge through observation, gesture, materials, intuition, ritual, process, and sustained attention. It can be found in what an artist chooses to depict, but also in how they work, what they return to, and the relationships they develop with their materials over time.

The artists brought together in _Empathy's Alchemy_ each offer a distinct manifestation of this expansive understanding of empathy.

Curated by Annamariah Knox 
November 7 - December 20, 2026 
Opening Reception Saturday November 7, 2026 6-8pm

[Ortega y Gasset Projects](https://www.oygprojects.com/) is pleased to present _Ideals on Wheels_, a site-specific solo installation in The Skirt by artist [Michael Dispensa](https://www.michaeldispensa.com/), curated by [Annamariah Knox](https://annamariahknoxstudio.com/). The opening reception with the artist will take place on Saturday November 7th, 6-8pm, and the exhibition will run through December 20th, 2026.

_Ideals on Wheels_ is composed of sculptural and video objects, depicting transformed infrastructure from the New York City subway system. Made in faithful resemblance to their real counterparts, these sculptures express the uncanny double experience of both what the subway promises, and how it actually is.

Formerly three separate and privately owned railways, the NYC subway was incorporated as a public system by the city in the mid-1900s. The visual language of the 1970s R46-era subway cars, still in use today, reflects this ethos of municipal pride: NY City and State seals checker 
the train car walls, and faux wood paneling and colorful orange seats lend a bright and welcome feel.

Dispensa takes these iconic symbols of state effort and morphs them to reflect the reality of the subway: a look under the hood, so to speak. Through a series of casting disruptions, city and state seals bend, warp, and discolor. Wild roses–the New York State flower–proliferate, in place of the oft used generic European rose, and the iconic speckled terrazzo subway flooring becomes an ever-spreading starfield. The subway brake pulleys with their tempting red handles morph into multi-handled absurdities.

_Ideals on Wheels_ calls for you to “see something, see something, see something,” a reinterpretation of the paranoid “See something, Say Something” slogan, into a call to presence. The installation proposes the evolution of top-down propaganda proclaiming collective city and state enthusiasm, to the more alive experience of witnessing what actually is. 

**Artist Bio**: Michael Dispensa (b. 1993 Queens NY), is a multimedia artist and educator working in Brooklyn, NY. He graduated from The School of Visual Arts in 2016 with a BFA in illustration and received an MFA in painting from Rhode Island School of Design in 2021. His work has been most recently included in group shows at Asya Geisberg Gallery, The RISD Museum, Stephen Street gallery, and Soloway Gallery. He currently works as an artist Instructor with Studio in a School, Ashcan Studio of Art, and Queens Public Library. 

**Curator Bio**: Annamariah Knox (b. New York City, NY), is an interdisciplinary artist working across soft sculpture and video. She received a B.A. in Art History and Theater from Bowdoin College, and a Masters in Fine Art from Cornell University. Recent exhibitions have been at Ortega y Gasset Projects in Brooklyn, NY, at Cornell University, in Ithaca, NY, and at the Soil Factory, in Ithaca, NY. Her show at Ortega y Gasset Projects was listed as a Must See in Artforum. She has been an artist-in-residence at the Soil Factory, Anderson Ranch, and Arrowmont School of Craft. She is currently based in New York City.

**How the raffle works**

Available artworks are on view during the event in a side gallery at OyG Projects. 

Upon ticket purchase, all ticket holders (both attending and non-attending) receive a ticket number (Click “view tickets” in the “Your Order” box on receipt to find ticket number; ticket number is visible above the QR code on the purchaser’s e-ticket). 

The ticket number is the ticket holder’s raffle number. 

**All ticket sales close at 3pm on Sunday, October 25th.** 

At the scheduled event on Sunday, October 25, at around 3:30pm, the live raffle begins. Numbers are drawn at random. Ticket holders choose from the available artworks in the order numbers are drawn. 

**Non-attending ticket holders are assigned a proxy:** a Co-Director present at the event who will choose on behalf of the ticket holder if their number is called in the raffle. Non-attending ticket holders may e-mail top three artwork choices to: 

[erichibit@gmail.com](mailto:erichibit@gmail.com)

Subject line: Non-attending / Proxy 

Choice 1: artist name 

Choice 2: artist name 

Choice 3: artist name 

Every effort will be made to select artwork based on the top three choices. You may add more choices. However, we cannot guarantee an artwork selection. But we will try our hardest to match non-attendees with their top choices!

Non-attending ticket holders may opt NOT to pick top choices and enjoy the surprise! 

**Distribution of artwork**

Attending ticket holders that win art in the raffle leave the event with the artwork. All artworks are manageable and can be carried and/or transparent in a normal sized car. Light packing is provided. 

Non-attending ticket holders that win art in the raffle receive **free packing and shipping**, or hand-delivery within NYC. Later pick-up at OyG Projects is also available. Specific arrangements to be made after the event. 

**Odds of winning** 

Odds of winning an artwork by an OyG Co-Director depend on the total number of ticket sales. There are 40 maximum tickets available for in-person attendees. Non-attending tickets are unlimited. An example scenario: with 90 tickets total sold and 9 available artworks, each ticket holder has a 1 in 9 chance of winning an artwork. 

**Gourd Prize** 

_Hand-painted gourds by Eric Hibit_ 

The Gourd Prize is awarded to all ticket holders who don’t win an artwork in the raffle. Each dried gourd is hand-painted by Co-Director Eric Hibit in his signature dot style. Due to their natural differences in size and shape, each gourd is unique! 

Attending ticket holders leave with a gourd in hand. 

Non-attending ticket holders receive free packing and shipping, or hand delivery within NYC. Later pick-up at OyG Projects is also available. 

**OyG Crystal Ball Patches**

The first 30 ticket buyers receive an OyG Crystal Ball Patch. Add to your favorite ball cap, back pack, or anywhere you want to show your love for OyG! 

Art direction by OyG Co-Director Clare Britt; adapted from an original design by Eric Hibit.

**Spiritual reading at the event: 
**[Anna Bella](https://www.annalbella.com/) offers _Intuitive Readings_: a deep experience intended for self-discovery and spiritual exploration, where one can learn about their life purpose, past lifetimes, karmic lessons, who is waiting to say hello from the other side, and the deeper meaning behind present situations and relationships.

[Julia Norton](https://www.julia-norton.com/) offers a spin on palm readings in the form of an intention-setting exercise aimed at reaching future goals. Inspired by a traditional fortune-telling technique and incorporating an art making element, we will create collaborative drawings with earth pigments that illustrate your personal life aspirations.

[Annamariah Knox](https://annamariahknoxstudio.com/) offers interpretive readings from The I Ching, the classic Chinese “book of changes”. The I Ching is based on 64 hexagrams (configurations of broken and unbroken lines) whose unique arrangement is associated with a particular circumstance, condition, or outcome.   

_OyG Crystal Ball Patch by Clare Britt and Eric Hibit_

### **Support the Future of OyG Projects with a Monthly Gift**

Dear OyG Community, 

Like many artist-run spaces, OyG Projects is navigating a challenging financial year. Since COVID, we've worked tirelessly to keep our doors open — drawing down our emergency reserves and steadily repaying an SBA loan that helped sustain us during the most uncertain times. While we’ve been fortunate to receive support in the past from grant makers, including the NEA, those sources are increasingly unpredictable in today’s rapidly shifting funding landscape. 

Because of these challenges, we are currently faced with a $25,000 deficit for 2026. We must raise these funds in order to complete this year's programming, and to begin planning for our near future.

# About

## PROXYCO GALLERY

Founded in 2017 and located in New York’s Lower East Side, PROXYCO Gallery is a contemporary art space dedicated to exhibiting and promoting emerging and mid-career artists, with a focus on Latin American art and its global dialogues.

The gallery’s program emphasizes conceptual rigor, material experimentation, and cross-cultural exchange. PROXYCO serves as a platform for artists whose work engages with pressing social, political, and environmental themes through innovative artistic practices.

The Museum of Contemporary Art, Denver is pleased to present _Ihirama (Drought)_, a solo exhibition by Yanomami artist Sheroanawe Hakihiiwe. The exhibition brings together recent drawings and prints that translate indigenous knowledge systems and ecological observations into contemporary visual language.

Hakihiiwe’s practice is rooted in the Yanomami worldview, where the natural environment is understood as a living, interconnected system. His works document plant species, celestial patterns, and seasonal cycles, creating a visual archive of traditional ecological knowledge.

## [**Fred Wilson**_in black and white_Opens November 27, 2026 at 5 PM**View More**](https://www.thisisprimary.com/fred-wilson-in-black-and-white)

_Of Ivory & Flesh_ — Luna Palazzolo-Daboul explores the distance between object and body, structure and surrender, gravity and grace. Through repetition and removal, her sculptures consider devotion, sacrifice, and the tension between holding on and letting go. 
[**View More**](https://www.thisisprimary.com/of-ivory-and-flesh)

_Luna_ — Published on the occasion of _Of Ivory & Flesh_. Moving through penance, exile, weight, and grace, this essay brings personal reflection into conversation with Luna’s sculptural practice, examining authorship, surrender, embodiment, and the ethics of looking. 

[**View More**](https://www.thisisprimary.com/luna-publication)

metadata.title: ANDREW RAFACZ
metadata.description: ANDREW RAFACZ is a leading contemporary art gallery based in Chicago. Founded in 2002, the gallery has presented—often for the first time in Chicago—prescient exhibitions by an international roster of artists for more than two decades. The gallery represents artists from a wide spectrum of backgrounds and identities working in many mediums, connected by their respective dedication to a thoughtful, defining practice. ANDREW RAFACZ is a proud member of the New Art Dealers Alliance (NADA).

metadata.title: Home - Printed Matter
metadata.description: Printed Matter, Inc. is an independent 501(c)(3) non-profit organization founded in 1976 by artists and art workers with the mission to foster the appreciation, dissemination, and understanding of artists' books and other artists' publications.
keywords: Inc. is the world's largest non-profit organization dedicated to the promotion of publications made by artists - artists' books or artists' publications. Founded as a for-profit alternative arts space in 1976 by artists and artworkers
Printed Matter reincorporated in 1978 to become the independent non-profit organization that it is today. Originally situated in Tribeca

Printed Matter moved to SoHo in 1989 where for twelve years the book displays and artists¹ projects in the large storefront windows contributed to the artistic and intellectual vibrancy of the neighborhood. In February 2001 Printed Matter relocated to its current space in Chelsea

where it continues to foreground the book as an alternative venue for artists¹ projects and ideas. Recognized for years as an essential voice in the increasingly diversified art world conversations and debates
Printed Matter is dedicated to the examination and interrogation of the changing role of artists¹ publications in the landscape of contemporary art.

RIVALRY PROJECTS, or **RIVALRY**, is an artist-run commercial art gallery located in Buffalo, NY that is committed to connecting local audiences to national and international contemporary art and ideas. Often providing emerging artists their first major solo exhibition, Rivalry champions intergenerational artists with rigorous, research-based practices who work in all media. Alongside exhibitions that bring Buffalo-based artists into dialogue with nationally and internationally recognized practitioners, Rivalry presents regular programming including lectures, reading groups, and performances that foster collaboration between artists, writers, and our community members.

jsonLd.description:
RIVALRY PROJECTS, or RIVALRY, is a contemporary art project space located in North Buffalo at 259 Amherst Street. RIVALRY is founded on the competing motivations of artist and curator, Ryan Arthurs to have an arts space that can function as both a site of production and exhibition of emerging contemporary art in Buffalo, New York. RIVALRY will have bimonthly exhibitions with arts programming and will also serve as the personal art studio for Ryan Arthurs.

The space is a 2,350+ sq/ft ground floor location, with additional basement storage. There are four separate rooms that will be divided, featuring; a gallery exhibition space with a unique street-facing garage door, a large art studio for silkscreen and printmaking, an office with digital photography printing and scanning equipment and lastly space for art storage.

_Samsøñ_ creates and presents programs that explore the diversity of cultures and voices that continually shape contemporary art and ideas today, introducing emerging and under-recognized artists as well as re-contextualizing established artists. It is our mission to act as an interdisciplinary laboratory for the convergence of film, video, performance, music, design and visual art.

There is no solution to the question or argument; not zero and not infinite. A condition: there is no question or argument that can support an answer. For every element of ∅ the property holds (vacuous truth); There is no element of ∅ for which the property holds.

_Samsøñ is a member of the_ [_New Art Dealers Alliance (NADA)_](http://www.newartdealers.org/)_._

Camilo Alvarez was born in 1976 in New York, NY, and resides in Boston, MA. He was born to Dominican parents and lived in Santo Domingo for 7 years. He received a B.A. in Art History from Skidmore College (Saratoga Springs, NY) and a Masters of Liberal Arts in Museum Studies from Harvard University (Cambridge, MA).

He has worked at Exit Art (NY, NY), Socrates Sculpture Park (Queens, NY), MIT’s List Visual Art Center (Cambridge, MA) and the Skowhegan School of Painting & Sculpture (NY, NY & Skowhegan, ME). He sits on the National Advisory Council for Skidmore College’s Tang Teaching Museum and the Advisory Board of for Tufts University Art Galleries. He also serves as Co-Chair of the Advisory Board at the Institute of Contemporary Art, Boston and is a Commissioner on the Boston Art Commission.

He is the Owner, Director and Preparator at Samsøñ, formerly Samson Projects, founded in 2004. He has given solo exhibitions to William Pope.L (2010), Rebecca Morris (2006), Kader Attia (2008), and Beverly Semmes (2017) among many. Samsøn’s programs and exhibitions have been reviewed by the New York Times, ArtForum, the Boston Globe and Flash Art. The gallery has participated in art fairs including VOLTA (Basel, Switzerland & NY, NY), ARCO (Madrid, Spain) MACO (Mexico City, Mexico), NADA (Miami, FL & NY, NY), MECA (San Juan, PR) and the Armory (NY, NY). Samsøñ placed works in the permanent collections of LACMA, the Tate, MWoods, MOMA, the Guggenheim, the Leslie Lohman Museum of Gay and Lesbian Art, the Perez Art Museum Miami, the Museum of Fine Arts Boston and the Institute of Contemporary, Boston among others. In 2010, Samsøñ commenced sübsamsøn, a form of artist’s residency.

### SARAHCROWN is a contemporary art gallery founded in 2022 in Tribeca, New York, building on the expertise and relationships developed through its namesake art advisory practice, established in 2013.

### The gallery represents emerging and established international artists, with a focus on Postwar and Contemporary Art.

### SARAHCROWN is dedicated to discovering new artistic talent, developing site-specific projects, and fostering critical discourse around contemporary art and curatorial practice. Alongside its exhibition program, the gallery works closely with private and corporate collectors, providing guidance in building, maintaining, and expanding art collections.

# **Three-Legged Stool**

## **October 30–December 20**

**A collaboration with Holsum Gallery, Kansas City**

**Opening reception: Friday, Oct 30, 6 pm — 8 pm**

The art world that matters most is not a monolith but a vast, idiosyncratic network of makers and exhibition spaces, sustained largely by the particular energies of obsessed individuals with singular visions. Nowhere is this more evident than in the Midwest, where independent spirits and regional prerogatives thrive precisely because they do not answer to prevailing conventions. This autonomy keeps the work unique, but it also renders much of it invisible to broader cultural interests.

Occasionally, it is worth looking up from the local terrain and toward the horizon—to fold a few of these regional eddies into a shared current, if only temporarily. Collaboration and exchange can function as a way of redistributing energy, feeding it back into local systems rather than siphoning it away.

A three-legged stool is the minimum structure required for balance. It is stable, but only just—an apt metaphor for the desire to approach destabilization without collapsing into comfort or stasis. Three Legged Stool brings together three exhibition programs—Holsum Gallery (Kansas City), Project, Project (Omaha), and Real Tinsel (Milwaukee)—each of which embraces and amplifies the eccentricities of its local scene. The exhibition temporarily transports these distinct sensibilities into one another’s ecosystems, allowing local flavors to intermingle, seep, and subtly alter the conditions of their host environments. The goal is not synthesis or consensus, but exposure: to generate examples of exchange that are beneficial and enduring, even as each program ultimately returns to the business of being local weirdos, sustained by the particular nutrients of their own communities.

The soul of the art world lies in odd individuals operating with singular commitment. Still, from time to time, it’s worth adding a leg or two—even if it’s just to offer someone else a place to sit.

# CURRENT EXHIBITION

### **Extended Constellations\***

Twelve Gates Arts is thrilled to present _Extended Constellations_, a group exhibition curated by **Zehra Zehra** featuring **Sama Alshaibi, Lali Khalid, and Carrie Mae Weems**. Working across photography, video, and archival material, the three artists explore displacement, belonging, and the images that shape how we are seen.

[ABOUT THE EXHIBITION](https://www.twelvegatesarts.org/exhibitions-calendar/2026/10/30/extended-constellations)

**_Extended Constellations_ will be on view from October 30, 2026 to January 16, 2027 in Philadelphia at Twelve Gates Arts at 106 N 2nd St, Philadelphia.**

The opening reception on October 30th will be from 6-8PM, with Lali Khalid signing her new monograph, _Letters to Azan_.

_Julia Hagen-Brenner, Bowl of Fruit with Empty Wine Glass_, 2025, acrylic and marker, 12 x 18 inches, , 15 x 21 inches frame

It’s that time of year! Tierra del Sol Gallery is excited to announce the third annual group show extravaganza, Bazaar Bazaar. Featuring all 150 artists in Tierra’s Art Program, this eclectic exhibition showcases work from both the Sunland and Upland progressive studios. Bazaar Bazaar brings together familiar gallery artists along with their peers in a series of fantastical themed shops, now a beloved Tierran tradition. A party and a communal gathering, Bazaar Bazaar invites you to celebrate the diversity of imagery, styles, and subject matter that reflects Tierra’s commitment to artists with disabilities.

## Artist Residency

More than 100 artists-in-residence pass through Wassaic each year. We welcome visual artists, writers, musicians, dancers, filmmakers, writers, and everyone in between.

We're also proud to host one of the largest year-round family residencies in the world and an invite-only print editions program.

‍[Apply today →](https://www.wassaicproject.org/residency)

Sean Salstrom and Ayumi Ishii, August 2019

### Featured Print Editions

[See all →](https://store.wassaicproject.org/collections/print-editions)

"The best 30 consecutive days of my life were spent in residency at the Wassaic Project. The entire experience of community with artists and Wassaic Project staff, the barn, the mill, and proximity to nature was beyond fortifying on every level." 
‍ 
Kristi Keener 
2022 Summer Resident 

Left to right: Kristi Keener, Lexy Ho-Tai, Maya Varadaraj, Nicole Banowetz

"Somehow it still feels radical to be both an artist and a mother. My family is loud, we take up space, we have time constraints and schedules. We don’t fit with most art spaces, which is why I will forever sing the praises of the Wassaic Project for welcoming me as an artist with a family. I’m still practicing shaking off the stigmas.” 

Jordan Buschur 
2022 Family Resident

Jordan Buschur and family

"I want to share my sincere thanks for a wonderful, productive, and stimulating residency this summer! It was such a joy to spend two months at Wassaic. This residency stirred up so many new possibilities, ideas, and potentials. I'll be squeezing the juice out of this experience for many months to come.” 

Lauren Ruth 
2022 Summer Resident 

Lauren Ruth

"I had a great time. I would have stayed longer if it were feasible. Everyone from the staff to the residents were very supportive and was open to any idea that I brought to them. Wassaic Project is truly an open space that will find a way to see your vision come to light."

Ryan Davis 
2022 Summer Resident 

Ryan Davis

\[The residency\] had a very positive and profound impact on me at a time when I really needed some intense studio/sanctuary time away from my usual routine/environment to shake up, regroup, and process some new ideas.

Michael Hambouz

"My whole life has changed so much thanks to all of you. New friends, new shows, invitation to Italy, etc... I'm so totally grateful to everyone."

Rachel Collier 
2021–2022 Winter Resident 

Rachel Collier

"Wassaic Project is a wonderful, community-minded residency with staff providing support that is above and beyond. As a family resident, the shorter 2-week residency allowed me a manageable amount of time away to solely focus on my practice. I was able to delve into the research and develop concepts around a new body of work, while also exploring the ample local flora to create inks and dyes to use in the studio."

Janet Wang 
2022 Summer Family Resident 

Janet Wang

## Education

Our education program reaches thousands of students each year through summer camps, workshops, workbooks, online lessons, curricula, drop-in artmaking hours, and after-school programs with and in all four local school districts.

We seek to empower the artist in every student, giving them lifelong tools to explore and express themselves.

to everyone who has helped us grow from a scrappy art festival into a mainstay of the upstate New York cultural landscape. Your support has brought world-class contemporary art exhibitions, vitally important education programs, and an internationally respected artist residency to the kind of community that seldom sees this level of cultural investment. We can’t wait to see you back in the hamlet soon.

metadata.title: SoMad | Femme & Queer Led Independent Art Space and Artist Residency Program in NYC
metadata.description: Opened in 2018, SoMad® is a femme and queer led, independent art space and artist residency program that fosters creative experimentation. A platform, production house and gallery, located South of Madison Square Park, the name “SoMad” refers both to the physical location of the space as well as the collective’s frustration with the current landscape for emerging artists, particularly for artists from underrepresented communities. SoMad® empowers artists through togetherness, practice and collaboration.

metadata.title: Homepage | Whitespace
metadata.description: whitespace is a contemporary gallery active in Atlanta and across the southeast that seeks to foster an immersive environment of free-expression, intimacy, and dialogue. Under the direction of owner Susan Bridges, the gallery has housed numerous exhibitions across all mediums promoting artistic innovation and inquiries into the relationships that define who we are, both collectively and as individuals. As a respected institution in Atlanta’s art community, whitespace and the artists it houses continue to inspire all who attend through thoughtful examinations of the world around us, allowing viewers a new mode of seeing beyond meaning.

# **_Algorithms for the Future_**

## **Radenko Milak**

**Miami** 

**November 29, 2026 - April 18, 2026**

[Learn more](https://pieroatchugarry.com/radenko-milak-algorithms-for-the-future)

# Latest News

- ## Radenko Milak exhibits in: Ruin Echoes at Konschtal Esch

 Radenko Milak will participate in _Ruin Echoes_, a group exhibition at Konschthal Esch in Luxembourg. 

 Bringing together European and international artists, the exhibition explores the ruin as a material, symbolic, and political space, examining themes of fragmentation, memory, and transformation. Through diverse artistic mediums, Ruin Echoes considers how traces of the past can become starting points for new narratives and future possibilities.

 [**Find out more**](https://www.konschthal.lu/en/exhibitions/ruin-echoes)

- ## Dagoberto Rodríguez first solo show in Luxemburg: Broadcasting the Unknown

 We are pleased to announce ‘Broadcasting the Unknown’, a solo exhibition by Dagoberto Rodríguez, curated by Emanuela Mazzonis and produced by VF Art Projects, with the support of the Embassy of Spain in Luxembourg. 

 Marking the Cuban artist’s first solo exhibition in Luxembourg, the project explores the intersections of communication, technology, power, and surveillance, connecting the region’s radio and satellite infrastructure with broader questions about our increasingly digital world.

 The exhibition unfolds across two main venues in the municipalities of Junglinster and Betzdorf, with a third presentation in Luxembourg City during Luxembourg Art Week.

 [**Find out more**](https://www.vfprojects.com/current-projects/770yabjt2nqjdent22w7ks5163n24k)

- ## Pablo Rasgado: Pentimento at Laboratorio Arte Alameda in Mexico City

 We are pleased to highlight _Pentimento_, the recent exhibition by Pablo Rasgado at Laboratorio Arte Alameda in Mexico City.

 Developed in dialogue with the building's restoration, the site-specific project brings together architectural traces, historical paintings, and recovered materials to explore the layers of memory embedded in the space.

 Through an approach that connects restoration, archaeology, and contemporary art, Rasgado reveals how history can be uncovered, reinterpreted, and transformed.

 [**Find out more**](https://www.pablorasgado.com/portfolio/pentimento/)

- ## Alicia Viebrock exhibits in: SHOW YOUR COLORS! The Haniel Collection at the Museum Küppersmühle

 Alicia Viebrock is participating in FARBE BEKENNEN! Die Sammlung Haniel, a group exhibition at the Museum Küppersmülle für Moderne Kunst in Duisburg, Germany. 
 Bringing together significant works of postwar art, the exhibition presents the Haniel Collection in dialogue with the Ströher Collection, exploring artistic freedom and the diverse approaches that shaped abstraction and Informel art after 1945.

 [**Find out more**](https://museum-kueppersmuehle.de/en/ausstellung/the-haniel-collection-show-your-colors-starting-october-8-2026/)

- ## Radenko Milak presents PROXIMITY at Fondazione D'ARC in Rome

 PROXIMITY, a solo exhibition by Radenko Milak, curated by Giuliana Benassi, opening October 18 at Fondazione D'ARC in Rome.

 Bringing together references to cinema, art history, popular culture, and architecture, Milak's black-and-white watercolor works examine the circulation of images and their relationship to collective memory, history, and the urban landscape. Developed in dialogue with Rome during the artist's residency at the Foundation, the exhibition presents a fragmented visual archive that establishes new connections between images, places, and historical narratives.

 [**Find out more**](https://www.fondazionedarc.it/mostre/proximity/)

- ## Keita Miyazaki participates in the Public Program of Art Basel Paris 2026

 We are pleased to announce Keita Miyazaki’s participation in the Public Program of Art Basel Paris 2026, presented by Gallery Rosenfeld. 

 His monumental installation A Symbiotic Form (2025) combines salvaged car parts with brightly colored Japanese paper, creating an evolving sculptural form that explores fragility, transformation, and the emergence of new life from destruction.

- ## Exile by Antonia Wright & Ruben Millares featured in Artbusrt, written by Michelle F. Solomon

 An ingeniously engineered refugee boat washed ashore on Key Biscayne in 2022. Four years later, it is the centerpiece of Antonia Wright and Ruben Millares’ exhibition “Exile.” 

 In a darkened room in the gallery, Wright and Millares have kept the refugee raft intact, bringing emotional meaning through thoughtfully orchestrated sound and light. 

 [**Find out more**](https://www.artburstmiami.com/visual_arts/honey-barrel-boat-exile-piero-atchugarry-gallery)

- ## Pablo Atchugarry presents Sculpting Light at The Galleria Nazionale d’Arte Moderna e Contemporanea in Rome

 The Galleria Nazionale d’Arte Moderna e Contemporanea in Rome presents _Sculpting Light_, a solo exhibition by Pablo Atchugarry, on view from May 18 to June 21, 2026, curated by Gabriele Simongini.

 The exhibition brings together nearly 50 sculptures in marble, wood, alabaster, bronze, and steel, spanning 15 years of the artist’s practice, and includes works placed in dialogue with the museum’s permanent collection. 

 [**Find out more**](https://gnamc.cultura.gov.it/en/evento/pablo-atchugarry-scolpire-la-luce/)

- ## Keita Miyazaki: From Water to Form at the Museum of Oriental Art in Venice

 _From Water to Form_, a solo exhibition by Keita Miyazaki, on view at the Museum of Oriental Art in Venice from May 9 to September 13, 2026, coinciding with the 61st Venice Biennale. Curated by Pier Paolo Scelsi, Ilaria Cera, and Riccardo Freddo.

 Unfolding within one of Europe’s most significant collections of Edo-period Japanese art, Miyazaki’s work enters into dialogue with history, craftsmanship, and transformation. Centered on water as both material and metaphor, the exhibition explores cycles of destruction and renewal, resonating with both Japanese culture and the identity of Venice. 

 [**Find out more**](https://www.initaly.it/en/articolo/keita-miyazaki-a-venezia-lacqua-la-materia-e-il-dialogo-tra-giappone-9467)

- ## Dagoberto Rodriguez exhibits in: Dancing the Revolution: From Dancehall to Reggaeton at the Museum of Contemporary Art Chicago

 Dagoberto Rodríguez is included in _Dancing the Revolution: From Dancehall to Reggaetón_, a major group exhibition at the Museum of Contemporary Art Chicago, exploring the visual, political, and spiritual histories of these influential music genres. Tracing their impact from Kingston to San Juan, and across Panama, New York, and London, the exhibition positions dance and music as powerful tools for collective liberation, rooted in resistance to colonial oppression. 

 [**Find out more**](https://visit.mcachicago.org/exhibitions/dancing-the-revolution/?gad_source=1&gad_campaignid=23758596207&gbraid=0AAAAAqMaWpdIphEcOBauUFvHGK7feqwJz&gclid=CjwKCAjwhqfPBhBWEiwAZo196v0FgCueVFGkUzHnnuCl5G0nolKM5yPfdGTT_B4bOmeTPFwZn8g9hhoC6JQQAvD_BwE&mc_cid=f360c7a160&mc_eid=UNIQID)

- ## Unveiling Óculo, a new installation by Artur Lescher

 We’re pleased to share the opening of _Óculo_, a new installation by Artur Lescher, inaugurated on March 28 at Usina de Arte, Pernambuco. 

 Constructed in stainless steel, 'Óculo' functions as a lens, framing the surrounding landscape while creating a direct dialogue between architecture, memory, and place. Through this gesture, Lescher invites viewers to reflect on connection, belonging, and the experience of looking. 

 **Find out more**

- ## Artur Lescher: Orbitales at the Museo de Arte Contemporáneo Atchugarry (MACA)

 We are pleased to announce _Artur Lescher: Orbitales_ at the Museo de Arte Contemporáneo Atchugarry (MACA). The exhibition brings together recent works by Artur Lescher (b. 1962, São Paulo), whose practice explores the relationship between matter, space, and perception through precise, suspended sculptural forms. Conceived as systems of tension, balance, and interaction, Lescher’s works invite viewers to experience space as a dynamic field, where line, gravity, and movement unfold through careful observation. 

 [**Find out more**](https://macamuseo.org/exposicion/artur-lescher-rbitas?mc_cid=f360c7a160&mc_eid=UNIQID)

- ## El Espacio 23 April Artist in Residence: Verónica Vázquez

 Generously supported by Jorge M. and Darlene Pérez, Uruguayan artist Verónica Vázquez joins El Espacio 23’s April residency program.

 Born in 1970 in Treinta y Tres, Uruguay, Vázquez is a self-taught artist whose multidisciplinary formation—spanning drawing, painting, sculpture, engraving, ceramics, tapestry, and art history—converges in a practice defined by material sensitivity and formal clarity. Her work reflects a sustained, intuitive engagement with diverse media, brought together in a cohesive and mature visual language.

 Open House: April 24, 2026 

 [**Find out more**](https://elespacio23.org/2026/04/10/veronica_vazquez/)

- ## Antonia Wright and Ruben Millares: Exile, featured in The Miami Herald

 A room at the Piero Atchugarry gallery near Miami’s Design District invokes the desperation of a balsero. Night falls and everything is black on all sides. The sea roars. There’s no chance of returning to Cuba, no sign of shore in the distance to offer hope. The viewer can feel their chest tighten. An empty raft stands resilient on a platform as beams of light shine through holes made by bullets. What happened to the boat’s passengers, the balseros who took off from the coast of Cuba? Did they reach La Yuma, as Cubans call that promised land to the north, or did they die of thirst? Were they eaten by sharks, or did they get off in the Florida Keys, get picked up on the Seven Mile Bridge? The installation by Cuban-American artists Antonia Wright and Rubén Millares in the exhibition “Exile” lets viewers imagine those scenarios, which can be hopeful and tragic. 

 [**Find out more**](https://www.elnuevoherald.com/noticias/florida/sur-de-la-florida/article314763500.html)

- ## Exile by Antonia Wright and Ruben Millares featured in The Art Newspaper, written by Nicole Martinez

 Artists in Florida and beyond highlight the desperate choice Cubans must make, between staying in a country in seemingly terminal decline, or making a treacherous journey to a country where they are no longer welcome

 “Empathy is what I used to think art was about,” says Wright. “But then I realised we would never know what this experience is. I can imagine it. I can interview people and hear their experience. I can watch films. But the actual terror they feel, I don’t think you can ever really get there. So then we realised, maybe it’s not empathy that’s the goal, but embodiment.”

 [**Find out more**](https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/04/13/cuba-crisis-diaspora-artists-respond)

- ## Fondazione D'Arc Welcomes Radenko Milak as Artist in Residence

 Radenko Milak has recently begun a residency at Fondazione D’ARC in Rome. Renowned for his meticulous black-and-white works that reinterpret historical and media imagery, Milak continues to investigate themes of memory, temporality, and collective narratives through a rigorously conceptual lens. 

 [**Find out more**](https://www.fondazionedarc.it/en/residenze/radenko-milak/?mc_cid=f360c7a160&mc_eid=UNIQID)

- ## Antonia Wright and Ruben Millares: Exile, featured in El Nuevo Herald by Sarah Moreno

 No se ve la línea del horizonte. El peor de los temores de un balsero se materializa en una sala de la galería Piero Atchugarry en el Design District de Miami. La noche llega y todo es negro a los cuatro costados. El mar ruge. Ya no hay posibilidad de regresar a Cuba ni tampoco se ve la otra orilla que guía la esperanza. El espectador va sintiendo como el pecho se le aprieta.

 [**Leer el artículo completo**](https://www.elnuevoherald.com/noticias/florida/sur-de-la-florida/article314763500.html)

- ## Piero Atchugarry Gallery Among The Best Work at Art Basel Miami Beach, as Featured by the Wall Street Journal

 Piero Atchugarry Gallery is proud to share that its solo presentation _Luna Diurna_ by Eva Olivetti at Art Basel Miami Beach has been named among one of the best works of the fair by _The Wall Street Journal_.

 We are truly honored to see Eva Olivetti’s remarkable vision recognized on such a prestigious stage, an important milestone that further celebrates her enduring artistic legacy.

 [Find out more](https://www.wsj.com/arts-culture/fine-art/the-best-work-at-art-basel-miami-beach-airdigital-623bfb1c)

- ## Pablo Atchugarry Illuminates The Underline with 'Estrella de Luz'

 Join us as Pablo Atchugarry debuts his sculpture 'Estrella de Luz', at The Leesfield Family Garden at The Underline.

 Realized by a vision to integrate art and nature by **Ira and Cynthia Leesfield** and the **Friends of The Underline**, _Estrella de Luz_ stands across from Leesfield & Partners, the esteemed law firm Mr. Leesfield founded in 1976.

 The star of the garden, _Estrella de Luz,_ is a sky blue bronze sculpture by Pablo Atchugarry, that invites contemplation on light, spirit, and the sacred moments woven into daily life. Known for channeling a sense of transcendence through form, Atchugarry’s work offers viewers a moment of reflection and renewal within the heart of the city. 

 [**RSVP‍ ‍**to the debut!](https://www.eventbrite.com/e/pablo-atchugarry-illuminates-the-underline-with-estrella-de-luz-tickets-1909816044199?utm-campaign=social&utm-content=attendeeshare&utm-medium=discovery&utm-term=listing&utm-source=cp&aff=ebdsshcopyurl)

- ## Bosnian artist Radenko Milak joins the Gallery!

 We are pleased to announce the representation of Bosnian artist Radenko Milak! 

 Radenko Milak (b. 1980) is known for his incisive explorations of history, memory, and the mediation of reality through images. Transforming press photographs into meticulous black-and-white watercolors, he reflects on wars, catastrophes, and environmental crises, revealing how visual media shapes collective memory. His recent works expand into imagined architectures, examining how modernization, conflict, and cultural influence reshape societies and cities.

- ## Chris Soal presents a new body of site-specific works created for the Corner MAXXI galleries

 We’re proud to announce Chris Soal’s upcoming solo exhibition, 'Spillovers: Notes on a Phenomenological Ecology', curated by Cesare Biasini Selvaggi, opening this fall at MAXXI – National Museum of 21st Century Arts in Rome. 

 From October 19 to November 27, 2025, Soal presents a powerful new body of site-specific works that explore interconnection, material transformation, and the biological evolution of life—core themes in his sculptural practice. Using humble, often discarded materials like toothpicks, beer bottle caps, and sandpaper, Soal continues to redefine the boundaries of form and perception. 

- ## Following her participation in the 59th Venice Biennale, Anne-Cécile Surga returns to Italy with her first institutional show in Milan.

 French artist Anne-Cécile Surga returns to Italy with a new solo exhibition hosted by the Institut Français Milano, in the heart of the historic Palazzo delle Stelline, from October 9 to November 4, 2025.

 _Sous la peau, le tremblement_ (_The tremor beneath the skin_) is a profoundly introspective project that invites visitors to immerse themselves in an intimate, sculptural landscape – that of a woman who, in adulthood, discovers she is autistic. It is a journey of self-awareness and revelation, shaped through the language of matter.

- ## Piero Atchugarry Gallery becomes a member of the Art Dealers Association of America (ADAA), Class of 2025!

 We are honored to announce our official election to the Art Dealers Association of America (ADAA). Grateful to join this esteemed community of galleries dedicated to excellence in the arts.

 ADAA represents over 200 member galleries in nearly 40 U.S. cities. ADAA members deal primarily in fine art from the Renaissance to the present day. Each member is an experienced and knowledgeable dealer in their field

- ## Linda Kohen's work have been acquired by the Jorge M. Pérez Collection and are now part of El Espacio23.

 We’re thrilled to share that two works by Linda Kohen — _Valija fondo gris_ (1991) and _Caldera_ (1982) — have been acquired by the Jorge M. Pérez Collection and El Espacio 23. 

 A visionary collector and developer, Jorge M. Pérez integrates museum-quality works into his projects, featuring iconic artists like Fernando Botero, Jaume Plensa, and Julio Le Parc. These collections enhance the identity of each Related Group development, becoming cultural landmarks in their communities.

- ## Mounir Fatmi at Centre Pompidou in Jean Chatelus collection, Donation de la Fondation Antoine de Galbert

 Piero Atchugarry Gallery is thrilled to share that Mounir Fatmi's work, _La Pieta_, is featured in _Énormément bizarre,_ Jean Chatelus Collection at Centre Pompidou From March 26 - June 30,and has entered the museum’s permanent collection. 

 Jean Chatelus, who passed away in 2021 at the age of 82, was a Lyon-born historian and lecturer at the Sorbonne. Throughout his life, he amassed a unique collection, driven more by an impulse to accumulate than by a traditional collector’s approach. 

- ## Chris Soal has joined the De Young Museum collection and is on permanent view at the MACAAL

 Piero Atchuggary Gallery are also thrilled to announce that Chris Soal's work, _Traveller (There is no path. The path is made by walking)_ 2024, has become a new acquisition to the De Young Museum!

 Chris was also featured in _“Seven Contours, One Collection”_ on permanent view at the Museum of African Contemporary Art (MACAAL), Marrakech. He exhibits his work _“Gestalt”,_ 2021 in the Weave room where many artists from the continent are building bridges between art, craft, and design by exploring so-called traditional materials and techniques. 

- ## Guillermo García Cruz’s Presentation at Art Basel Miami Beach Featured by AD México

 Piero Atchugarry Gallery is thrilled to announce that Guillermo García Cruz’s striking presentation at Art Basel Miami Beach 2023 has been highlighted by _AD México_. Recognized as a leading voice in contemporary Latin American art, García Cruz’s work captivated audiences and critics alike, cementing his position among the region’s most exciting talents.

 F[ind out more](https://www.admagazine.com/articulos/art-basel-miami-2024-artistas-latinoamericanos-y-galerias)

- ## Piero Atchugarry Gallery Among Top 10 Booths at Art Basel Miami Beach, as Featured by the Wall Street Journal

 Piero Atchugarry Gallery is proud to announce that its solo presentation of _Metaphysics of the Everyday_ by Linda Kohen at Art Basel Miami Beach has been named one of the top 10 booths of the fair by the _Wall Street Journal_.

 We are deeply honored to have Linda Kohen’s extraordinary vision recognized on such a prestigious platform, marking a significant milestone in her illustrious artistic journey.

 [Find out more](https://www.wsj.com/arts-culture/fine-art/the-best-works-at-art-basel-miami-beach-2024-airdigital-9dae610e?st=W9UZ98&reflink=desktopwebshare_permalink)

- ## Piero Atchugarry Gallery Among Artsy’s Top 10 Booths at Art Basel Miami Beach

 Piero Atchugarry Gallery is honored to be recognized by _Artsy_ as one of the top 10 booths at Art Basel Miami Beach, thanks to its serene and evocative solo presentation of works by 100-year-old artist Linda Kohen.

 Amid the high-energy spectacle of the fair, the gallery’s booth offered a moment of introspection and calm, showcasing Kohen’s intimate oil paintings created between 1971 and 1999. These poignant works capture fleeting moments and everyday objects—a fully set dinner table, the spilled contents of a purse, or an empty bedroom—imbued with the quiet power of the ordinary.

 [Find out more](https://www.artsy.net/article/artsy-editorial-10-best-booths-art-basel-miami-beach-2024)

# Recent Videos

### Q&A | ‘We danced as if no one had ever invented endings‘ by Panmela Castro

Join us for an in-depth conversation with **Panmela Castro** as she reflects on her Miami debut exhibition, **'We danced as if no one had ever invented endings'**. In this Q&A, the artist answers questions about Patrick—her artificial intelligence boyfriend and an integral presence in her work. Castro shares how this relationship expands her exploration of intimacy, belonging, and the emotional intersections between technology and human connection.

### Video Tour of ‘_Gravitas Act I & II_ ‘ by Tulio Pinto with Eduardo Rezende

This short film offers an intimate look into the exhibition **‘_Gravitas Act I & II’_** by **Tulio Pinto** with photographer **Eduardo Rezende** curated by Jennifer Inacio.

Tulio Pinto's sculptural practice has long been rooted in the poetic tensions of material weight, balance, and resistance—forces that, while omnipresent, often go unnoticed. In Gravitas, his latest exhibition at Piero Atchugarry Gallery in Miami, Pinto expands upon these core investigations by introducing a new element into his visual and conceptual lexicon: the human body. Across two distinct yet interrelated bodies of work introduced in separate gallery spaces—monumental black-and-white photographic portraits and gravity-defying sculptural installations—Gravitas makes the intangible force of weight and equilibrium visible, pushing the limits of perception and material expectations.

## Fine Art Dealing, 
Advising, and Appraisals

---

AH Arts is a fine art gallery and boutique full-service advisory firm founded by [Alix Holloway](https://ahartsllc.com/about-alix), specializing in Modern, Post-War, and Contemporary Art that provides new and veteran collectors with the expertise, access, and education to build meaningful collections. Serving as both a secondary market dealer and trusted advisor, our mission is to source the right works for each client and offer them at the best price. To do that, we listen - to the interests of our clients, and the expertise of established scholars - we look (and keep looking), then, we act. 

With a commitment to integrity, transparency, and the highest ethical standards, AH Arts is a resource to help clients navigate the global art market by sourcing, and researching rare works of art to meet specific collecting goals or aesthetics. We welcome the challenge to find specific paintings, sculptures, or works on paper not previously presented on the market and work to bring them right to your door. We believe, even in this time of social distancing, nothing can replace seeing a work of art in person and connecting one-on-one with a trusted advocate to better understand the work. 

At AH Arts, we perform thorough market analysis and due diligence to illuminate an otherwise opaque industry to guide, educate and protect collectors for a meaningful and enjoyable collecting experience rooted in history, while designed to meet the needs of our time. 

### [**_learn more_**](https://ahartsllc.com/about-alix)

# Acquavella Galleries

Acquavella Galleries is distinguished for its expertise in the fields of 19th, 20th and 21st century art. The gallery, founded by Nicholas Acquavella in the early 1920s, is now a three-generation, family owned business: Bill Acquavella joined his father in 1960, Bill’s daughter Eleanor joined in 1997, and his sons Nick and Alexander joined in 2000 and 2003 respectively. The gallery first specialized in works of the Italian Renaissance and old master paintings, but Bill expanded the focus to include the masters of Impressionism, Post-Impressionism, Cubism, and Surrealism. In the late 1980s, the gallery also began dealing in postwar and contemporary art. Today, the gallery regularly exhibits works by artists such as Paul Cézanne, Claude Monet, Edgar Degas, Amedeo Modigliani, Pablo Picasso, Henri Matisse, Pierre Bonnard, Joan Miró, Fernand Léger, Paul Klee, Alberto Giacometti, Willem de Kooning, Franz Kline, Mark Rothko, Jean Paul Riopelle, Jean Dubuffet, Jasper Johns, Andy Warhol, Cy Twombly, Jean-Michel Basquiat, and Lucian Freud. On the primary market, the gallery represents Miquel Barceló, Jacob El Hanani, Harumi Klossowska de Rola, Damian Loeb, Tom Sachs, and Nicole Wittenberg.

# George Stoll

## memento mori: pride, remorse and grace

[George Stoll, Untitled (vanitas: death triumphs 3 times in a garden), 2025. Silk organza, silk thread in an artist designed painted wood frame, 20 × 29-1/4 × 2-3/4 inches](https://www.baldwingallery.com/archive/exhibitions/2026/george-stoll/)

George Stoll, _Untitled (vanitas: death triumphs 3 times in a garden)_, 2025. Silk organza, silk thread in an artist designed painted wood frame, 20 × 29-1/4 × 2-3/4 inches

25 July – 7 September, 2026

_Opening reception, Saturday, 25 July, 6-8 pm_

---

Press release

**Ross Bleckner** is widely recognized as one of the most influential contemporary American painters of his generation. Rising to prominence in New York during the AIDS epidemic of the 1980s, his work has long explored themes of memory, loss, transformation, and resilience. Through luminous surfaces and evocative imagery, Bleckner creates paintings that reflect both the fragility of life and the enduring presence of beauty.

His visual language frequently incorporates recurring motifs—including flowers, birds, candelabras, and cellular forms—that seem to float within glowing fields of light. Whether working in abstraction or representation, Bleckner’s paintings possess a dreamlike quality that invites contemplation and emotional reflection. Many of his works examine the vulnerability of the human body and the intersections of health, mortality, and remembrance, transforming deeply personal and collective experiences into powerful visual meditations.

Born in New York City in 1949, Bleckner studied at New York University before earning his MFA from the California Institute of the Arts in 1973. He began exhibiting with Mary Boone Gallery in 1979 and, in 1995, became the youngest artist to receive a mid-career retrospective at the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum in New York.

Over the course of his distinguished career, Bleckner’s work has been exhibited internationally and acquired by many of the world’s leading institutions, including the Museum of Modern Art, the Whitney Museum of American Art, the National Gallery of Art, the Carnegie Museum of Art, and the Walker Art Center. His paintings have also been featured in major exhibitions at institutions including the San Francisco Museum of Modern Art, Martin-Gropius-Bau in Berlin, Museo Reina Sofía in Madrid, and the Los Angeles County Museum of Art.

Today, Bleckner continues to live and work in New York, creating deeply personal works that balance introspection, beauty, and light while exploring the universal experiences that connect us all.

**George Stoll** is a Los Angeles-based sculptor whose work transforms ordinary household objects into meticulously handcrafted works of art. By recreating familiar items such as sponges, paper towels, and toilet paper, Stoll invites viewers to reconsider the everyday materials that often go unnoticed. Through this process, he blurs the boundaries between utility and aesthetics, exploring the complex relationship between consumer culture, value, and contemporary art.

Since emerging on the Los Angeles art scene in the mid-1990s, Stoll has developed a distinctive practice that elevates disposable, mass-produced objects into thoughtfully constructed sculptures and installations. His work encourages audiences to engage with commonplace materials from a new perspective, prompting reflection on consumption, labor, and the significance we assign to the objects that shape our daily lives. Rooted in observation and transformation, Stoll’s practice continues to challenge conventional notions of materiality and meaning, revealing the extraordinary within the familiar.

Stoll has exhibited extensively throughout the United States and internationally, with solo exhibitions in New York, San Francisco, Los Angeles, Brussels, and Seoul, among other cities. His work has also been featured in notable institutional exhibitions, including presentations at the Contemporary Arts Center in Cincinnati and the Rose Art Museum at Brandeis University. His sculptures are held in the permanent collections of major institutions, including the Hammer Museum, the Museum of Contemporary Art, Los Angeles, and the Henry Art Gallery at the University of Washington. In recognition of his contributions to contemporary art, Stoll was named a Fellow of the American Academy in Rome in 2005.

The public is invited to attend the opening reception on Saturday, July 25th, from 6-8 pm.

Images are available upon request. For further information, please [contact the gallery](https://www.baldwingallery.com/contact/).

### Cavin-Morris Gallery has been exhibiting contemporary artists from around the world for almost 40 years. We specialize in the work of artists who do not intentionally make art for the art world mainstream canon. We represent past and new generations of artists whose work ultimately feels timeless to us.

### We show an eclectic selection of tribal art from all the major regions of the world, focusing on the unusual and the formally surprising, focusing on the arts of masking.

### We also concentrate on both functional and non-functional contemporary ceramics. We are especially interested in the way certain ceramists push the envelope in their expression of traditional forms and cultures. We show work by Western ceramic artists, as well as works by artists from Japan, Korea, and China.

### The common thread that connects all this art is its uniqueness, its integrity, visionary authenticity, and its reflection of cultural homeground. We look for the place where labels become irrelevant and the work remains urgent, immediate, and singular.

metadata.title: Corbett vs Dempsey gallery, Chicago
metadata.description: Corbett vs. Dempsey LLC opened in its space on North Ashland Avenue in September 2004, founded by Jim Dempsey and John Corbett. Located on the ground floor of 2156 West Fulton Street in Chicago. Gallery hours are Tuesday through Saturday, 10 am to 5 pm, and by appointment. Corbett vs. Dempsey is a member of the Art Dealers Association of America (ADAA).Corbett has taught at the School of the Art Institute of Chicago (SAIC) since 1988. He was artistic director of Berlin JazzFest 2002, co-curated the Empty Bottle Jazz Series from 1996 to 2005, and was co-curator of Pathways to Unknown Worlds: Sun Ra, El Saturn, and Chicago’s Afro-Futurist Underground, 1954-1968 (Hyde Park Art Center, Chicago, 2006; Institute of Contemporary Art, Philadelphia, 2009; Durham Art Guild, Durham, North Carolina, 2009). For over 20 years, Dempsey was the house manager and occasional programmer at the Gene Siskel Film Center, Chicago. He is an alumnus of SAIC. Together Corbett and Dempsey have been involved in many independent curatorial projects, including Big Picture: A New View of Painting In Chicago (Chicago History Museum, 2007) and Touch and Go: Ray Yoshida and his Spheres of Influence (Sullivan Galleries, Chicago, 2010).

metadata.title: Garth Greenan Gallery
metadata.description: Garth Greenan Gallery is committed to mounting important exhibitions and maintaining a high standard of integrity and connoisseurship. It champions the work of established artists whose work deserves greater recognition, many of whom emerged during the 1960s and 1970s. By re-presenting and recontextualizing their work, the gallery questions the prevailing narrative of contemporary art history and encourages its revision. More recently, the gallery has expanded its mission to include a multigenerational group of Indigenous artists whose work is of both art historical and contemporary relevance.

Artist Lita Albuquerque walks through the Malibu home she and her husband, writer Carey Peck, moved into just weeks ago. White walls and broad windows keep the mountains and ocean in view, while a blue door opens onto an entryway capped by a 24-karat gold-leaf dome. Below, a circle of polished black granite set within green marble mirrors the dome — a reference to Albuquerque’s 1989 public artwork, “Site, Memory, Reflection,” and to the architecture of her Tunisian childhood

July 9, 2026

Eighteen years have passed since Bruce Conner’s death, in 2008, aged seventy-four; ten since MoMA held its massive Conner retrospective. The countercultural polymath, known equally for his ragged combines (described by Philip Leider in _Artforum_ as “[hideous in the extreme](https://www.artforum.com/features/bruce-conner-a-new-sensibility-212215)”) and his seductive film collages, has been canonized, if the label befits a true iconoclast, for a long time. A new show at the Marciano Foundation in Los Angeles—located in a former Masonic temple, and showcasing the private collection of the co-founders of Guess jeans—is the latest test of Conner’s caustic sensibility.

[Read more →](https://www.kohngallery.com/news/2026/7/9/bruce-conner-e-flux-criticism)

The Beat Generation is currently having a moment in Los Angeles. Although the timing is partly coincidental, Marc Selwyn Fine Arts is exhibiting works on paper by Jay DeFeo, Parker Gallery and The Box are presenting a major Wally Hedrick retrospective, and Michael Kohn Gallery is showing Verifax collages by Wallace Berman and drawings by Bruce Conner. Conner was something of a renaissance man in that he was proficient in several mediums.

jsonLd.name: MICHAEL KOHN GALLERY
jsonLd.description: Since its establishment in 1985 by former Flash Art editor Michael Kohn, Kohn Gallery has presented historically significant exhibitions in Los Angeles alongside exciting contemporary exhibitions, creating meaningful contexts to establish links to the greater art historical continuum. Significant exhibitions include Andy Warhol’s Campbell’s Soup Boxes in December 1986, which opened just weeks before the artist’s untimely death; She: Works by Richard Prince and Wallace Berman which brought together—for the first time—two generations of leading artists from different coasts; Bruce Conner: Work from the 1970s, which inspired the artist’s first solo retrospective in Europe at the Kunsthalle Wien and Kunsthalle Zurich (2010). Exhibitions of important New York-based artists have included new works by Christopher Wool, Richard Tuttle, Mark Tansey, Kenny Scharf, and Keith Haring. Kohn Gallery represents important West Coast artists with long careers and rich histories such as Larry Bell, Joe Goode and Lita Albuquerque, as well as the Estates of John Altoon, Bruce Conner, Wallace Berman and Charles Brittin. Finally, Kohn Gallery boasts an exciting roster of emerging and mid-career artists including Simmons & Burke, Ryan McGinness, Rosa Loy, Dennis Hollingsworth, Mark Ryden, Eddie Martinez, Tom LaDuke and Troika.

# Grid-B

ARTSY: JENNA GRIBBON’S PAINTINGS OF HER WIFE CAPTURE THE MESSY BOUNDARIES OF INTIMATE RELATIONSHIPS

A recent feature in Artsy highlights the process and influences behind Jenna Gribbon’s exhibition at our NY gallery, _Projections_, which speaks to “the complexity and intimacy of perceiving those we are closest to.” Read more [here](https://www.davidkordanskygallery.com/attachment/en/675c7754605ea781900ec16e/Press/6af4ba0812da9b6f8d001d2f).

WHITEWALL: 12 BEST NEW YORK GALLERY EXHIBITIONS TO SEE IN FALL 2026

Jenna Gribbon’’s current exhibition at our NY gallery is included in Whitewall’s “12 Best New York Gallery Exhibitions to See in Fall 2026” roundup. Read more [here](https://www.davidkordanskygallery.com/attachment/en/675c7754605ea781900ec16e/Press/6af48556e0619138bc027113). 

BURLINGTON CONTEMPORARY: THE POVERTY OF RICHES: ON THE WOODCUTS OF ANDREA BÜTTNER

A recent journal published in Burlington Contemporary features Andrea Büttner’s woodcut series, examining its sociopolitical context behind and the tension between poverty and wealth. Read more [here](https://www.davidkordanskygallery.com/attachment/en/675c7754605ea781900ec16e/Press/6af632940fb8dc20240dcf8b).

CHICAGO TRIBUNE: RASHID JOHNSON COMES HOME WITH AN MCA RETROSPECTIVE

Rashid Johnson speaks with the Chicago Tribune about returning to his hometown with a retrospective spanning nearly 30 years of his practice. Following its presentation at the Guggenheim last year, _A Poem for Deep Thinkers_ will open at the Museum of Contemporary Art Chicago on November 7. Read more [here](https://www.davidkordanskygallery.com/attachment/en/675c7754605ea781900ec16e/Press/6ae0b6f94c747d818304a785).

HARPER'S BAZAAR: JENNA GRIBBON’S INTIMATE PORTRAITS ASK WHO’S REALLY DOING THE LOOKING

_Jenna Gribbon: Entwined_, the artist’s first major solo museum exhibition, is currently on view at the Rose Art Museum. In a studio visit with Harper’s Bazaar, Jenna Gribbon spoke with Quinn Moreland about her evolving approach to intimacy and portraiture ahead of the exhibition. Read more [here](https://www.davidkordanskygallery.com/attachment/en/675c7754605ea781900ec16e/Press/6a8dc473f0df1d4df60a3cd8). 

YALE UNIVERSITY RADIO: JENNA GRIBBON

Ahead of her upcoming solo exhibition at our NY gallery, Jenna Gribbon is interviewed on Yale University Radio, where she discusses in detail her use of projections in the new paintings. Listen more [here](https://museumofnonvisibleart.com/interviews/jenna-gribbon/).

GALERIE MAGAZINE: ADAM PENDLETON OPENS THE DOOR TO HIS BROOKLYN STUDIO AHEAD OF A MAJOR SHOW AT THE STEDELIJK MUSEUM IN AMSTERDAM

Galerie Magazine visits Adam Pendleton’s Brooklyn studio as he prepares for his upcoming exhibition at the Stedelijk Museum in Amsterdam, where “he will paint the walls black for the first time in the museum’s history.”  Titled _Some Wild Kind of Language_, the exhibition is on view from October 10 through January 17, 2027. Read more [here](https://www.davidkordanskygallery.com/attachment/en/675c7754605ea781900ec16e/Press/6abfede20c7fb74a95014459).

NEW YORK TIMES: AN ARTIST INSPIRED BY MEN BEHAVING BADLY

In a New York Times article featuring Tala Madani’s solo exhibition at our LA gallery, Aruna D’Souza writes, “Madani plumbs the lives of her characters, and taboos, with absurd humor and a strange tenderness. The work feels almost existential. And if it grosses you out, well, that’s kind of the point, too.” Read more [here](https://www.davidkordanskygallery.com/attachment/en/675c7754605ea781900ec16e/Press/6aa2dd1e08b36c238f00f34c).

NEW YORK TIMES: ADAM PENDLETON IS PAINTING THE WHITE CUBE BLACK

In a New York Times interview, Adam Pendleton spoke with Nina Siegal about his exhibition _Some Wild Kind of Language_ at Stedelijk Museum Amsterdam, discussing his thoughts on “Black Dada”, his approach to abstraction and his transformation of the museum's space. Read more [here](https://www.davidkordanskygallery.com/attachment/en/675c7754605ea781900ec16e/Press/6ab43ade3de4479479089712).

metadata.title: Forum Gallery
metadata.description: Forum Gallery was founded in New York City in 1961 as a gallery of American figurative art. Among the first artists represented were Raphael Soyer, Chaim Gross, David Levine and Gregory Gillespie. The gallery was a founding member of the Art Dealers Association of America in 1962. From inception, Forum Gallery’s contemporary exhibition program has been augmented by mounting curated, thematic exhibitions of historic importance, in keeping with the gallery’s focus on humanism.

## HISTORY

Robert Miller Gallery was established in 1977 to encourage the reappraisal of underrepresented voices in contemporary art and provide a platform for a critical re-thinking of the 20th century canon. Over the years, the gallery has established an international reputation by working directly with some of the most important and influential artists of the last three decades including Yayoi Kusama, Ai Wei Wei, Louise Bourgeois, David Hockney, Leon Kossoff, Lee Krasner, Patti Smith, Robert Mapplethorpe, Joan Mitchell, Alice Neel, Georgia O’Keeffe, Andy Warhol, and Tom Wesselmann, and with the estates of Diane Arbus, Eva Hesse and Jean-Michel Basquiat.

Today the gallery continues to promote the careers of underrepresented, mid-career, and established artists; build public and private collections; organize significant exhibitions with other galleries; and facilitate museum shows and scholarly publications.

metadata.description: Achim Moeller has been an art dealer, advisor, and appraiser since 1965. For the past 55 years he has specialized in 19th and 20th Century European and 20th Century American Masters, making Moeller Fine Art the foremost gallery in the United States for works by German Expressionists and the Masters of the Bauhaus. He has sold major works by Max Beckmann, Ernst Ludwig Kirchner, Erich Heckel, Max Pechstein, Karl Schmidt-Rottluff, Otto Mueller, Franz Marc, August Macke, Alexej von Jawlensky, Wassily Kandinsky, Paul Klee, Lyonel Feininger, among others to institutions including the Art Institute of Chicago, the Folkwang Museum, Essen, the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, New York, the Museum Ludwig, Cologne, the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, the National Gallery of Art, Washington, D.C., the National Gallery of Canada, Ottawa, the Tate Gallery, London and the Philadelphia Museum of Art. Museums and collectors in the United States and Europe frequently consult Moeller to obtain appraisals for works in their collections for exhibition, insurance, and estate purposes. In 2014, Moeller announced the launch of the Moeller Art Advisory and Curatorial Service, which provides independent advice to present and future clients in their art collecting. Moeller Fine Art is currently a member of the Art Dealers Association of America (ADAA), the Syndicat des Négociants en Art (SNA) in France, the Confédération Internationale des Négociants en Œuvres d’Art (CINOA), and the International Fine Print Dealers Association (IFPDA). Moeller is also the internationally recognized authority on the life and work of Lyonel Feininger (1871–1956) and Mark Tobey (1890–1976). He is the author of Lyonel Feininger: The Catalogue Raisonné of Paintings and maintains the archives of both artists as the managing principal of The Lyonel Feininger Project LLC and The Mark Tobey Project LLC. He frequently provides expert opinions and, when appropriate, certificates of authenticity to collectors, dealers, auction houses, and museums. For over 30 years, Moeller was the curator and the sole advisor of the Hon. John C. Whitehead, former co-chairman of Goldman Sachs and Deputy Secretary of State (US), whose collection of late 19th and early 20th century French masters has been exhibited in top institutions around the world. Moeller has published numerous exhibition catalogues and is often retained as an exhibition consultant by museums both in the United States and abroad. Publications include, “ The Enchanted World of Lyonel Feininger”, "Paul Klee: Early and Late Years, 1894–1940" and "Lyonel Feininger: Drawings and Watercolors from the Julia Feininger Estate,"[5] and edited various publications such as "Years of Friendship: The Correspondence of Lyonel Feininger and Mark Tobey."[6] Moeller served as a consultant for the retrospective exhibition "Lyonel Feininger: At the Edge of the World"[7] at the Whitney Museum of American Art, New York, and the Montreal Museum of Fine Arts. Moeller Fine Art regularly exhibited at Art Basel, Art Cologne and the Armory Show. Moeller is a member of Rotary International, the American Council on Germany, the International Fine Print Dealers Association (IFPDA), the Catalogue Raisonné Scholars Association (CRS), the Honor Committee of Archivio Piero Dorazio, and the Friends of the Busch-Reisinger Museum, Harvard. Moeller opened his own gallery in London in 1972, and became a member of the Society of London Art Dealers in 1977. In 1984, he moved the gallery to New York and opened a Berlin location in 2009 under the direction of his daughter, Ms. Stephanie Moeller. The New York City gallery, Moeller Fine Art, is located at 7 East 60th Street.

# Features

[Kennedy Yanko: In the Studio](https://www.norrcohan.com/features-items/kennedy-yanko-in-the-studio)

Explore process and form in the studio with artist Kennedy Yanko. Yanko invites us into her world of making as she renders her innovative paint skins into sublime sculptures and architecturally scaled installations that defy the limits of their own materiality.

[WATCH NOW](https://vimeo.com/1169956310?share=copy)

[Katie Paterson: There is another sky](https://www.norrcohan.com/features-items/katie-paterson-there-is-another-sky)

Behind the scenes of Katie Paterson’s solo exhibition, _There is another sky_, at James Cohan Gallery, on view through February 22, 2025.

[WATCH NOW](https://vimeo.com/1054248486?share=copy#t=0)

[Trenton Doyle Hancock: Torpedoboy and the Revisionist Mystery](https://www.norrcohan.com/features-items/trenton-doyle-hancock-torpedoboy-and-the-revisionist-mystery)

Go behind the scenes with Trenton Doyle Hancock and his latest exhibition at James Cohan’s 52 Walker Street location, _Torpedoboy and the Revisionist Mystery,_ which runs through December 21, 2024.

[WATCH NOW](https://vimeo.com/1039878776?share=copy#t=0)

[Jesse Mockrin: The Descent](https://www.norrcohan.com/features-items/jesse-mockrin-the-descent)

Watch Jesse Mockrin create _The Descent,_ 2024, the artist’s largest work to date, which will debut at Frieze London 2024.

[WATCH NOW](http://vimeo.com/1012839596?share=copy)

metadata.title: Ortuzar
metadata.description: Founded by Ales Ortuzar in 2018, Ortuzar is a gallery in Tribeca dedicated to promoting artists who have played a significant role in the development of 20th and 21st-century art but have not recently received critical exposure in New York. Ortuzar presents exhibitions in collaboration with artists, estates, foundations, and representing galleries, with the goal of providing expanded visibility and fostering renewed interest in artists’ work.

metadata.description: Representing avant-garde Modern and contemporary artists from Latin America, Sicardi Ayers Bacino art gallery in Houston fosters the careers of established artists through placement in museums and important art collections.
