metadata.title: Jack Shainman Gallery
metadata.description: Jack Shainman Gallery has been dedicated from its inception to championing artists who have achieved mastery of their creative disciplines and are among the most compelling and influential contributors to culture today. For nearly four decades, the Gallery has earned a reputation for introducing international artists to American audiences, and for promoting and developing young and mid-career artists who have gone on to gain worldwide acclaim, presenting the first New York exhibitions of artists including Nick Cave, Hayv Kahraman, Meleko Mokgosi, Richard Mosse, Toyin Ojih Odutola, Hank Willis Thomas, and Lynette Yiadom-Boakye, among many others. Today, Jack Shainman Gallery is celebrated for its multicultural roster of emerging and established artists and estates who engage in the social and cultural issues of their time. The Gallery was founded in 1984 in Washington, D.C. by Jack Shainman and Claude Simard (1956-2014). Soon after opening, the Gallery relocated to New York City, first in the East Village before moving to Soho and finally, in 1997, to its current location at 513 West 20th Street in Chelsea. In 2013, the Gallery opened two additional exhibition spaces, one in Chelsea at 524 West 24th Street, and another in a converted 30,000 square foot building in Kinderhook, NY known as The School.

metadata.description: Leslie Tonkonow Artworks + Projects is a contemporary art gallery located in New York City at 401 Broadway in the Tribeca art gallery district. The gallery specializes in modern and contemporary art from the 1960s to the present, created in a wide range of mediums including drawings, prints, paintings, sculpture, photography, and video. The gallery represents a roster of internationally recognized artists and Estates. It organizes group and solo exhibitions, selling works by gallery artists and others, and promotes the careers of represented artists by placing works in museum and private collections, through advertising, press outreach, and working to secure public art commissions.

# Online Exhibition - William Hogarth, Select Prints: A Private Collection

It is not an overstatement to characterize William Hogarth as pioneering and revolutionary. For his time he was avant-garde, cutting-edge, and shocking in his depiction of audacious subject matter. Trained as both a printmaker and painter, it was his prints that enabled him to reach and scandalize a domestic and international audience. Several series of his etchings – in particular, _A Rake’s Progress, A Harlot’s Progress, Marriage à la Mode and Gin Street, Beer Lane_ – moralized, titillated, and with their massive popularity and commercial success brought Hogarth and English art its first widespread recognition beyond England’s own shores.

The material in this catalogue is the complete private collection of Hogarth prints formed by a discerning American collector, Herbert M. Schiller, M.D. Dr. Schiller did most of his buying in the 1990’s in London. The major sets and most of the major individual prints are represented.

Vielmetter Los Angeles is thrilled to announce Edgar Arceneaux and Hayv Kahraman will be included in the 13th SITE SANTA FE International Biennial: _There Are Other Worlds_ curated by Ekow Eshun. Opening June 11, 2027, _There Are Other Worlds_ brings together artists from around the world to explore imagination, possibility, and new ways of seeing in uncertain times. Featuring new commissions by Edgar Arceneaux, Firelei Báez, Sanford Biggers, Raven Chacon, Hayv Kahraman, Lotus L. Kang, Cauleen Smith, and others.

New Mexico provides both the setting and an important point of departure for _There Are Other Worlds_. The region’s layered histories of Indigenous presence and displacement, migration, cultural exchange, and artistic experimentation offer a rich context in which to consider how different worlds might materialize.The Biennial places contemporary artistic practices in conversation with New Mexico’s distinctive cultural histories, convening artists from around the world who explore issues of belonging, transformation, survival, ecology, and the future.

“Bringing the Biennial to Santa Fe again is an opportunity to connect artists and ideas from around the world with a place that has such a deep and distinctive history of artistic experimentation,” said Louis Grachos, Phillips Executive Director of SITE SANTA FE. “We’re excited to present the thirteenth iteration of the Biennial and to welcome this incredible group of artists to Santa Fe.”As with the previous International Biennial, _There Are Other Worlds_ will extend beyond SITE SANTA FE to various locations throughout the city. Together, these venues will invite audiences to experience the Biennial across a range of cultural and architectural contexts.

@graph.description: Vielmetter Los Angeles is a contemporary art gallery founded in 2000 by Susanne Vielmetter. It represents a roster of local and internationally recognized artists and develops long-term relationships with them. Since 2019 the gallery has been located at 1700 S Santa Fe Ave #101 in Downtown Los Angeles, with exhibition spaces Gallery I–IV, a Viewing Room, the Greenhouse and the Lanai. The gallery showed early solo exhibitions of artists including Amy Sillman and Edgar Arceneaux (2002), Rodney McMillian and Wangechi Mutu (2003) and Mickalene Thomas (2007). Earlier gallery locations were on Wilshire Boulevard (2000–2005) and in Culver City (from 2004), complemented by a project space in Berlin (2007–2009).

## Worthington Gallery and Pocket Option: Exploring the Intersection of Art and Investment

Worthington Gallery, founded in 1970 by Eva-Maria Worthington, has long been a beacon for German Expressionism and other avant-garde art movements. Specializing in major movements like Blaue Reiter, Bauhaus, Neue Sachlichkeit, and Naive Art, the gallery has earned a reputation for presenting works of renowned artists such as Max Beckmann, Ernst Barlach, and Horst Janssen. But beyond its role in the art world, Worthington Gallery's engagement with contemporary topics, including art as an investment, presents an interesting intersection with platforms like Pocket Option.

### The Gallery?s Influence on Art Investment

Worthington Gallery's exhibitions, which often focus on the history and significance of German Expressionist works, have educated countless collectors and investors about the cultural and financial value of art. Over the years, the gallery has hosted numerous landmark exhibitions and has provided valuable context for collectors looking to invest in pocket option desktop app rare and unique pieces. This knowledge-driven approach resonates well with platforms like Pocket Option, a broker known for offering access to global financial markets. Pocket Option allows investors to trade assets, including commodities and stocks, much like art investors analyze the potential of high-value pieces over time.

### Bridging the Gap: Art as an Asset

The connection between Worthington Gallery?s art expertise and financial platforms such as Pocket Option can be seen in the growing trend of art as an asset. Investors now look beyond traditional stocks and bonds to diversify their portfolios, considering art investments as a viable option. The expertise of Worthington Gallery in curating exhibitions and providing educational insights about the value of Expressionist works aligns with the growing interest in rare assets?whether it be through the purchase of physical art or digital representations such as NFTs.

Just as Pocket Option allows individuals to explore the financial potential of a variety of assets, art collectors and investors can gain significant returns from works presented by galleries like Worthington. As the art market continues to evolve, the merging of traditional art appreciation and modern financial platforms will only grow, offering exciting opportunities for art lovers and investors alike.

mainEntity.name: Where are David Zwirner gallery locations?

acceptedAnswer.text: David Zwirner operates gallery spaces in New York (Chelsea at 19th & 20th St, and Tribeca at 52 Walker), Los Angeles (Melrose Hill), London (Mayfair), Paris (Le Marais), and Hong Kong (H Queen's).

mainEntity.name: Are David Zwirner exhibitions free to visit?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, all gallery exhibitions across David Zwirner locations globally are free and open to the public during normal operating hours.

mainEntity.name: How can collectors acquire artwork or fine art prints from David Zwirner?

acceptedAnswer.text: Artworks, limited-edition prints, and publications can be inquired about and acquired through David Zwirner's digital viewing rooms and exhibitions, Utopia Editions print shop, or by contacting the gallery sales team.

mainEntity.name: Does David Zwirner accept artwork consignments?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, David Zwirner accepts consignments for secondary market artworks by gallery-represented artists and estates through their dedicated Collect and Consignments program.
